> **[promoted: the sync-semantics verdict → architecture.md §Bot decisions ARE seed-reproducible — "do not route bot decisions through `SharedRandom`": `LocalRandom` is excluded from `World.SyncHash()` (folds only Actors + `ISync` + synced effects + `SharedRandom.Last`), bots emit orders not RNG draws, and moving draws into `SharedRandom` would shift every combat roll and break the frozen `@stable` A/B baseline recorded on the seeded-`LocalRandom` build `2d3c8fe0`. The seeding FACT itself was already promoted there. Verified `World.cs:217/:225-228/:283-286/:540-554`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

A tasking asked to decide the right fix for "same-seed bot games diverge because `World.cs:214` leaves `LocalRandom` unseeded" (citing the 2026-07-19 finding). That premise is **stale**: the fix shipped ~2 weeks ago and the cited line numbers (213/214) predate it. No new code was written; this entry is the verdict + the sync-semantics reasoning so the question is not re-opened a third time.

- **Current state (verified, `main` @ 18ff375b):** `World.cs:217` seeds `SharedRandom = new MersenneTwister(RandomSeed)`; `World.cs:225-228` seeds `LocalRandom = new MersenneTwister(DeriveLocalSeed(localSeed))` when `localSeed != 0`, else falls back to the wall-clock ctor. `DeriveLocalSeed` (`World.cs:283-286`) is the canonical PCG64 LCG `x*6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407` truncated to int32. Landed at `2d3c8fe0` (2026-07-20, verdict_version 5) and refined at `d71dd48b` (2026-07-24). Pinned by `engine/OpenRA.Test/OpenRA.Game/SeedDerivationTest.cs` (constants + truncation + golden vector `DeriveLocalSeed(1017)==894286612` + no-fixed-point + injectivity + stream-divergence). Already promoted to `architecture.md` "Bot decisions ARE seed-reproducible".
- **Sync-semantics argument (why (a) is safe and (b) is not):** (1) `LocalRandom` is excluded from the sync hash — `World.SyncHash()` (`World.cs:540-554`) folds only Actors and `ISync` fields, and the RNG contribution elsewhere is `SharedRandom.Last` only — so its seed value never participates in desync detection and reseeding it cannot change multiplayer sync. (2) Bots tick client-side (`ModularBot.cs`) and emit choices as **orders** through the order pipeline; orders — not the RNG that produced them — are what synchronize peers and replays, so a differently-seeded `LocalRandom` changes which orders a bot issues but never breaks lockstep. (3) The two MersenneTwisters are independent, so seeding `LocalRandom` does not touch the `SharedRandom` stream (combat rolls, projectile inaccuracy, damage) at all — @stable/Normal/legacy/human sim behavior over the synced stream is byte-identical. (4) Option (b) (route bot decisions through `SharedRandom`) is the WRONG fix precisely because inserting bot draws into the shared stream would shift every subsequent combat roll and break the frozen @stable A/B baseline's RNG-stream identity — the exact invariant a prior influence-stack defect already tripped. (5) The decorrelating transform (vs. reusing the raw seed) keeps decision rolls statistically independent of combat rolls while staying a pure function of the lobby seed, and the `!= 0` guard preserves wall-clock nondeterminism for normal launches so real games are not accidentally same-seeded.
- **@stable byte-identity is intact, not at risk:** the frozen A/B benchmark baseline was recorded ON the seeded-`LocalRandom` build (`2d3c8fe0` is described as "the first paired-comparison" baseline), so the seeding is already baked into the baseline — there is nothing to shift. The bot modules that still draw from `LocalRandom` are the stock/legacy squad + base-building modules (`SquadManagerBotModule`, `UnitBuilderBotModule`, `BaseBuilderQueueManager`, `McvManagerBotModule`, `CaptureManager`/`CaptureCoordinator`, `PoiOffensive`/`PoiGarrison` reeval countdowns, `HelicopterSquadBotModule`, `MinelayerBotModule`, `SupportPowerBotModule`, `HarvesterBotModule`, `Squad.cs:62` aliases `World.LocalRandom`), and they DO run for @stable — but seeded, so per-seed reproduction holds and the baseline is unperturbed.
- **@experimental influence stack stays zero-RNG:** the belief/danger/territory/frontline traits (`BeliefStore`, `DangerFieldLayer`, `ControlField`, `SightingThreatLayer`, `EngineerRouteOpenBotModule`, `LaneAmbushBotModule`, `StancePositioningExecutor`) draw **zero** `SharedRandom`/`LocalRandom` by design (SharedRandom only staggers a first tick in a couple); this fix does not add any RNG to that path and does not change it.
- **VERDICT: HOLD — no code.** The unambiguous-safe option is already in `main`; a worktree/build/test cycle would produce an empty diff. Delivered as written verdict only, per the "if implementing changes nothing you cannot rule out, deliver the verdict" clause. (Did not build, did not run tests, did not run any game/autotest.)

## 2026-08-03 — The heli transport drop-site picker is the ONE transport drop that uses the omniscient `ThreatMap.FindWeakestEnemyCell` (not the fog-legal MountedTransport path) — root cause of "drops land behind the enemy SR" (air-polish, `auto/air-polish`)

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §@experimental consumers beyond D/E/F — new "Heli transport drop-site reshaping" consumer (`RiskWeightedDropSite`): the heli drop was the one transport drop still committing to the raw omniscient `ThreatMap.FindWeakestEnemyCell`, now reshaped fog-legally by `TransportDropSiteMath.ScoreDrop` over believed control depth + danger + own-SR distance (weight not filter, candidate-source omniscience precedented); plus the `FlightPathHysteresis` order-cadence damper. Verified `HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:263/:246/:944/:1022`, `ThreatMapManager.cs:232`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Polishing the bot air/transport subsystem surfaced a drop-site asymmetry worth pinning:

- **`HelicopterSquadBotModule.TryLaunchTransportMission` picked its drop zone as `threatMap.FindWeakestEnemyCell(player)`** (`HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:~886`, pre-change), gated only by `GetThreat(weakCell) < 50`. `FindWeakestEnemyCell` (`ThreatMapManager.cs:232-273`) scans EVERY grid cell for enemy presence and returns the one with the **lowest total enemy Cost** — so a lone cheap enemy unit sitting deep behind the enemy Supply Route reads as the globally "weakest" cell and is selected, landing the infantry drop somewhere unreachable and lethal. It is a fully OMNISCIENT scan (`world.FindActorsInCircle` with a relationship filter, no fog check).
- **This is the opposite discipline from `MountedTransportBotModule`**, whose drop candidate comes from the omniscient `GetFrontline`/`GetFriendlyInfluence` but is then **post-adjusted fog-legally** by `ApplyStandoff` off the believed danger field (see influence-stack.md §consumers beyond D/E/F). The heli path had no such fog-legal reshaping — it committed to the raw omniscient pick.
- **Fix (experimental, default-off `RiskWeightedDropSite`):** rank a candidate set (the weak cell + top `PoiMap.GetOffensiveTargets` POIs) by `TransportDropSiteMath.ScoreDrop`, a fog-legal penalty over believed-enemy control DEPTH (`ControlField.ScoreAt` — negative = enemy; the enemy-SR anchor floors a radius-4 disc to ≈ −800, a strong "behind the enemy SR" signal), believed danger (`DangerFieldLayer.GroundDanger`/`AirDanger`) and Chebyshev distance from our own SR (reachability). A WEIGHT not a filter (nothing hard-banned). The omniscient weak cell stays a *candidate* (candidate-source omniscience is precedented); only the reshaping term is belief-side, so the fog-legality merge-block is satisfied.
- **Both attack-heli order-issue sites that churn under @experimental are in the FSM states, not the module:** the standoff `AttackMove` re-issue (`HelicopterApproachState`) and the withdraw `Move` re-issue every tick for 75 ticks (`HelicopterWithdrawState`). The withdraw loop is the loudest — it re-issued a Move each tick to a per-tick-recomputed retreat cell (esp. the `RandomBuildingLocation` fallback jitters). Flight-path hysteresis (`HeliPathHysteresis.ShouldRetarget`, default-off `FlightPathHysteresis`) damps both by holding the committed leg until the recomputed cell shifts ≥ threshold (or the leg completes). Order-cadence only — the destination is still chosen by the standoff/danger-nav/frontier logic, so the first-contact AA gate, strategic pin, and evacuation are structurally untouched (they live on other code paths).

## 2026-08-03 — Engineer bridge-repair with `EnterBehaviour.Dispose` consumes the engineer AT HUT-ENTRY, while the bridge stays `Dead` through the repair animation — a route-open mission must gate "repair in progress" (`hut.Repairing`) BEFORE its engineer-died-en-route failure check, or every success is misrecorded as a failure (frontline-influence Phase 6, `auto/frontline-p6`)

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging (new Phase-6 bullet: `EngineerRouteOpenBotModule` as a ledger-committed consumer — avenue.Cell == hut.Location resolution, identify-engineer-by-trait, `bridge-repair`/`bridge-screen` ledger keys) + Consumers table P6 row; the `EnterBehaviour.Dispose` engineer-consumed-at-hut-entry lifecycle gotcha (bridge stays Dead while `hut.Repairing`; gate repair-in-progress BEFORE the failure check) → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise. Verified `RepairsBridges.cs:31/:66-72/:92-118`, `LegacyBridgeHut.cs:32`, `BridgeHut.cs:240` (both `Repairing` public), `CrossingMap.cs:744-745`, `ControlField.cs:829`, `EngineerRouteOpenBotModule.cs`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Wiring `EngineerRouteOpenBotModule` (dispatch an `e6` to a repairable destroyed flank bridge when the P4 profile says that sector is the weakest enemy sector) surfaced the load-bearing lifecycle facts:

- **The `RepairsBridges` engineer (`e6`) uses `EnterBehaviour.Dispose` (`RepairsBridges.cs:31`), so the engineer actor is REMOVED when it enters the hut — before the bridge finishes repairing.** During the repair the hut's `BridgeDamageState` is still `Dead` but `LegacyBridgeHut.Repairing`/`BridgeHut.Repairing` is true (`LegacyBridgeHut.cs:32`, `BridgeHut.cs:240`, both public). A mission tick that reads "bridge still Dead + engineer gone ⇒ failure" therefore fires a FALSE failure (with cooldown + a wasted retry) on a mission that is actually succeeding. The fix: check `IsBridgeRepairing(hut)` and hold (keep the screen committed, wait for the bridge to flip to not-Dead ⇒ success) BEFORE the engineer-alive and timeout gates. Ordering is the whole safety property, mirroring the P5 posture-hold-after-retreat-gate discipline.
- **A repairable avenue's `Cell` IS the bridge hut's `Location`.** `CrossingMap.RevalidateCrossings` records a repairable `GroundCrossing` with `CellX/CellY = hut.Location` (`CrossingMap.cs:744-745`), and `ControlField.AddAvenue` carries that straight into `FrontlineAvenue.Cell` (`ControlField.cs:829`). So the consumer resolves the hut actor by exact `a.Location == avenue.Cell` over `world.Actors` filtered on `LegacyBridgeHutInfo`/`BridgeHutInfo` — no separate hut→avenue map needed.
- **Identify the engineer by TRAIT, not name list.** `actor.Info.HasTraitInfo<RepairsBridgesInfo>()` is the robust "this unit can open a bridge" test (survives faction/name variants `e6.america`/`e6.russia`); the `e6` is already in the bot's build list (`ai-america.yaml`/`ai-russia.yaml`, weight 20 / limit 2) and excluded from every other bot module, so nothing competes for it and NO purchasing hook is needed — the bot already owns engineers.
- **The RepairBridge order is `new Order("RepairBridge", engineer, Target.FromActor(hut), false)`** (`RepairsBridges.cs:66-72/:92-118`, `Target.Type == Actor`); `bot.QueueOrder` resolves it on the engineer, which queues the `RepairBridge` activity (walk-to-hut + enter + repair). No custom activity needed.

## 2026-08-03 — Phase-5 posture-hold must ride the retreat FSM's fall-back path, not become a new order writer — the safety property "never blocks a genuine retreat" is STRUCTURAL only if it is placed AFTER the retreat gate that already returned (frontline-influence Phase 5, `auto/frontline-p5`)

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging (new Phase-5 bullet: man-the-line `AllocateAcrossAvenues` coverage-then-largest-remainder, weakest-point ×100 bias, sector posture-hold; the posture-hold-safety-is-POSITIONAL discipline — three `CommitAndOrder` fall-back gates in order retreat→damper→posture-hold, each RETURNS before the mission-commitment snapshot; `SectorOfTargetCell` shared column-bucket helper; `AvenuesForSector`-allocates-fresh-List ⇒ read `Avenues` once per scan) + Consumers table P5 row. Verified `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:1244/:1622/:1639/:1653/:1671`, `FrontlineAllocationMath.cs:56`, `ControlField.cs:977-979`, `LayeredDefenceBotModule.cs:539/:585`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Wiring man-the-line + weakest-point + posture-hold (`FrontlineAllocationMath` + `LayeredDefenceBotModule`/`PoiOffensiveBotModule`) surfaced two integration constraints worth pinning:

- **Sector posture-hold is a HOLD trigger, and its "never blocks a losing retreat" guarantee is positional, not conditional.** `PoiOffensiveBotModule.CommitAndOrder` runs three gates in order: (1) genuine retreat (`CombatRetreatMath.ShouldRetreat`, `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:~1528`) — RETURNS for a `Retreating` axis; (2) retreat-oscillation damper (`DamperShouldHold`); (3) NEW posture-hold (`PostureShouldHold`). Because (1) already returned for any genuinely-losing axis, placing (3) *after* it means posture-hold can only ever fire on a NON-retreating axis — the safety property is guaranteed by ordering, with no re-check needed. Posture-hold reuses the SAME `OrderRetreat(stagingAnchor ?? rallyCell)` grouped fall-back the retreat/damper use, so it composes with the FSM (one fall-back order stream) instead of fighting it; it must also run BEFORE the mission-commitment snapshot + RETURN, or a held axis would be marked `Committed` and `PartitionHeldAxes` would freeze it holding forever (same discipline the retreat/damper gates already follow).
- **A target's frontier sector is a pure column-bucket of its map-cell X, reusable across both consumers.** `FrontlineProfileMath.SectorOfMapCellX(cell.X, ControlField.Info.CellSize, ControlField.GridWidth, ControlField.FrontlineSectorCount)` maps any objective cell to the same sector index the P4 profile is keyed on — so the weakest-point bias (does this target sit in the thin sector?) and posture-hold (is this target's sector overmatched?) share one helper (`SectorOfTargetCell`) and never need the ControlField's internal grid. Fog-legal (map geometry only), zero RNG.
- **`ControlField.AvenuesForSector` allocates a fresh `List` per call (P4 adversarial note); the man-the-line consumer therefore reads `ControlField.Avenues` ONCE per scan and buckets per-avenue in a single pass (`TryBuildAvenueData`), never calling `AvenuesForSector` per-unit.** `Avenues` is map-static + deterministically ordered, so the allocation (`FrontlineAllocationMath.AllocateAcrossAvenues`: coverage-first, largest-remainder surplus on the outnumbered avenues) is reproducible without touching the per-call allocation.

## 2026-08-03 — A Phase-4 sensor gated on the ControlField world trait would NOT be byte-identical: @stable now PARTICIPATES in the influence stack, so the profile flag must be a per-@experimental-player opt-in, not a world-trait/world.yaml global (frontline-influence Phase 4, `auto/frontline-p4`)

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging (Phases 0–4) + §Participation — the `@stable`-now-PARTICIPATES correction (fixed the stale "excluded" claim) + the per-player-opt-in gating recipe for a new read on a shared world layer; CrossingCells vs repairable Crossings avenue union. Verified `InfluenceStack.cs:47-48`, `ControlField.cs:280/:500/:579/:933`, `CrossingMap.cs:427/:453`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Building the frontline strength profile (`FrontlineProfileMath` + `ControlField` extension, `ControlField.cs`) surfaced the load-bearing gating subtlety for anything hung off the always-on world layers:

- **`InfluenceStack.Participates` returns true for @stable too** (`InfluenceStack.cs:48`, since the 2026-08-02 @stable→@experimental parity promotion). So @stable DOES get a `PlayerControl` and DOES run `RecomputePlayer`. A naïve "gate the new work by a flag on `ControlFieldInfo` set in `world.yaml`" would therefore build the profile for @stable (and for humans, who also participate for the overlay) — breaking the "byte-identical for @stable / normal / human" invariant. The `MinFrontierDistanceCells`/`FrontierDistance` precedent is *not* a counter-example: that array is built for ALL participants unconditionally, and byte-identity there only holds because @stable/human building the same deterministic array doesn't change a *non-participant* game — but a NEW per-participant array is extra state inside the @stable sim itself.
- **The fix: a per-player opt-in.** `ControlField.RequestFrontlineProfile(player)` adds the player to a `HashSet<Player>`; `RecomputePlayer` builds the profile only for members. The master flag lives on `PoiOffensiveBotModuleInfo.FrontlineProfileEnabled` (default false — the `ForwardStagingEnabled` pattern, set true only in the `@experimental` ai.yaml block, no @stable twin ⇒ C# false inherits), and the @experimental module calls `RequestFrontlineProfile` once when resolving its ControlField ref. @stable/normal/human never set the flag ⇒ never opt in ⇒ `profileEnabled` empty for them ⇒ zero profile work, byte-identical. This is the general recipe for ANY future per-@experimental-only read on a shared world layer that @stable now shares.
- **`CrossingMap` exposed crossing-cell COUNT but not the cells, and repairable (destroyed-bridge) crossings are NOT in `crossingCells`** — destroyed-bridge cells are water, so the geometric span detector never adds them; they live in `Crossings` (`GroundCrossing` with the hut's `CellX/CellY`). Avenue mapping therefore unions two sources: `CrossingMap.CrossingCells` (intact spans, newly exposed in `CrossingMap.cs`) tagged `Intact`, plus `CrossingMap.Crossings[].Cell` tagged `Repairable`. Both are map-static geometry, so the crossing→sector association is player-independent and refreshed at most once per tick.

## 2026-08-03 — Through-crossing DISTANCE (not binary reachability) is the lever that de-concentrates River-Zeta axes; barrier detection must use a NON-fording graph, and `tracked` is split by MOUNTAINS not the river (frontline-influence Phase 1.5, `auto/frontline-p01`)

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging (through-crossing distance provider + water-terrain barrier detection + locomotor water table). Verified `PoiReachability.cs:71`, `CrossingMap.cs:336/:459`, `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:768-778`, `world.yaml` TRACKED/LIGHTTRACKED/FOOT. NIT confirmed: the shipped barrier keys on water TERRAIN TYPE, not foot-impassability.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Wired `PoiReachabilityMath.ThroughCrossingDistanceCells` into `PoiMap.GetOffensiveTargets` distance (gated `Func<CPos,int?>` provider, null ⇒ exact Euclidean ⇒ byte-identical off) and validated with the one granted `test-frontline-reachability` rerun (verdict pass). The `[crossingmap]`/`[exp-reach]`/`[exp-reach-dist]` logs gave three concrete facts:

- **`tracked` is split into 3 ground components on River Zeta by MOUNTAINS, not the river.** `[crossingmap] built ground=3 infantry=1 amphibious=1`. `Locomotor@TRACKED` (`world.yaml`) has NO `Rock` terrain speed → `Rock` (mountain) is impassable for tracked, so mountain ranges disconnect the tracked graph; `foot` has `Rock: 50` and fords the river band, so the infantry graph is a single connected component. So neither the (fording) `tracked` NOR the (mountain-crossing) `foot` graph cleanly represents "the river as a barrier" — a component-count of the army locomotor is the WRONG signal for river-crossing distance.
- **Barrier detection must key on a NON-fording reference, and it works.** `CrossesGroundBarrier` walks the straight SR→POI line and flags any cell impassable for the non-fording `foot` locomotor (deep river/water; `foot` has no `River`/`Water` speed). `crossingCells=10` (foot-passable land cells spanning foot-impassable water on opposite sides, clustered) and `barrierCrossed=7`/11 POIs — the geometry detector found the real fords and the far-bank POIs. `foot` being connected overall does NOT stop per-line barrier detection (foot routes AROUND the water; a straight line still crosses it).
- **The lever materially de-concentrates the axis distribution.** Far-bank POIs' crow-flies distance is replaced by the through-crossing detour: e.g. `oilb@56,26` crow-flies ≈46 from SR@14,45 → `dist=65` (`score` 6.44M), `oilb@76,35` → `dist=64` (6.44M), while same-bank `oilb@19,76`/`@15,3`/`@25,22` keep crow-flies (`dist=30/42`, `score` 30M/24M/33M) — near-bank POIs now outrank the far-bank cluster by ~4–5×. The USA-bot's actual axes over the run were `supplyroute@80,35` (enemy-SR Pressure, top score) + near-bank west `oilb@17,44`/`@25,22` — i.e. secure the own bank + pressure the enemy SR, NOT lunge across the river at the far-bank central-crossing targets that raw crow-flies made look adjacent. (Caveat: no in-run flag-off A/B — the evidence is the inflated `dist`/reduced `score` on `crossesBarrier=True` POIs vs the unchanged same-bank ones, plus the resulting near-bank axis set.)
- **The reachability FACTOR stays inert here (`reach=Same` for all POIs)** because SR + all POIs sit in the same `tracked` component (the river is fordable, the mountains don't separate them), so the DISTANCE lever is the sole active mechanism — confirming the earlier finding that River Zeta's central-focus is a distance-metric artefact, not hard unreachability.

Kept `GroundLocomotor: tracked` default (component classification / reach factor); the barrier/distance path deliberately uses the `foot` (infantry) graph for the "is this land" side of a crossing span, and the actual water TERRAIN types (`Info.WaterTerrainTypes = {Water, River}`) for the barrier itself (adversarial NIT-A: keying the barrier on foot-IMpassability misreads cliffs/walls as water; keying on terrain type does not, and is unchanged on River Zeta whose foot-impassable line cells ARE River/Water). `lighttracked` ground A/B remains a documented follow-up.

**Metric note (adversarial optional NIT):** `CrossingMap.ThroughCrossingDistanceOverride` measures cell-space (`CVec.Length` = `ISqrt(dx²+dy²)` in cells) while `PoiMap`'s default distance is world-space (`WPos.Length/1024`). These are numerically the same quantity to within sub-cell rounding (a cell delta of (dx,dy) gives `WPos.Length = 1024·ISqrt(dx²+dy²)`), and the override only fires when the through-crossing detour is *tens* of cells longer than crow-flies, so the ≤1-cell metric discrepancy is immaterial to the DistanceFactor bucket. Left un-unified deliberately: the provider only has the POI's `CPos` (not its `CenterPosition`), so matching `PoiMap`'s WPos math exactly is not a two-line change and would not move any ranking.

## 2026-08-03 — River Zeta's ground graph is CONNECTED for the `tracked` locomotor (it fords River): the far-bank "unreachability" premise is weaker than assumed — the real central-focus lever is through-crossing DISTANCE, not binary reachability (frontline-influence Phase 0/1, `auto/frontline-p01`)

> **[promoted (durable subset) → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging — the locomotor water table (tracked fords River, lighttracked river-blocked, foot no-water/crosses-Rock) + `CrossingMapInfo.GroundLocomotor` tunable + reachability-inert-when-one-component. The River-Zeta-specific run observations are ephemeral, not banked. Verified `world.yaml`, `CrossingMap.cs:324`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Building CrossingMap (Phase 0) + reachability-gated POI scoring (Phase 1) and running the ONE budgeted observation autotest on real River Zeta (`test-frontline-reachability`, verdict pass) surfaced a correction to the research doc's Symptom-1 root cause:

- **The `tracked` locomotor can FORD rivers.** `world.yaml` `Locomotor@TRACKED` lists `River: 10` (nonzero ⇒ passable), and `RiverShallow: 75`; only deep `Water` (absent from `tracked`) is impassable. So with `GroundLocomotor: tracked` (the CrossingMap default), the `[exp-reach] reeval` log shows **all 12 River-Zeta oil-derrick POIs classify `Same`** (one connected ground component) — the river is not a hard barrier for tracked units, and the binary reachability penalty is correctly **INERT** on River Zeta (byte-identical there). The gate bites only on maps with genuine deep-`Water` barriers (or a `River`-terrain barrier under a River-blocked representative locomotor).
- **Representative-locomotor choice is load-bearing and army-dependent.** `lighttracked` (bradley / m109 / m270 — the bulk of the offense free pool) is River-blocked (`RiverShallow: 75` only, no `River`), `tracked`/`heavytracked` ford (`River: 10`/`5`), amphibious locomotors add `Water`. `tracked` (default) over-estimates reachability for the actual army; `GroundLocomotor: lighttracked` is the more army-faithful representative to A/B on a future budgeted run. `CrossingMapInfo.GroundLocomotor` is a tunable seam for exactly this.
- **Amphibious axis-typing is dormant with stock rosters.** Every amphibious unit (`m113`, `bmp2`, `btr` — all `*-amphibious` locomotors) is a troop carrier (`Cargo`/`Passenger`), so `UnitRoleResolver.IsTroopCarrier` excludes them from the offense free pool (`PoiOffensiveBotModule.IsEligibleCombatUnit`). `HasAmphibiousPool()` therefore returns false whenever the pool is pure MainBattle line units, and `ShouldTypeAmphibious` never fires — correct (don't type an amphibious axis you can't crew), but it means the amphibious branch only activates when an amphibious *MainBattle* unit exists (a future roster/Phase-2 change).
- **Implication for the plan:** Symptom 1 ("center-only, flanks neglected") on River Zeta is driven by the **crow-flies DISTANCE underestimation** (a walk-around/ford path is much longer than the straight line, but `PoiMap` distance ignores it), NOT by hard unreachability. The natural Phase-1.5 lever is wiring the **through-crossing / actual-path distance** (`PoiReachabilityMath.ThroughCrossingDistanceCells`, implemented + pinned but not yet applied to scoring) into `PoiMap` distance, so far-bank POIs read their true (longer) distance and stop scoring as if adjacent.

CrossingMap itself built on real River-Zeta terrain with no error and the reshape engaged every offense reeval, so the Phase-0 substrate + Phase-1 gating pipeline are validated end-to-end; only the *split-detection outcome* is map/locomotor-specific. (NOTE: the machine's OpenRA `Logs/debug.log` is SHARED across worktrees — a concurrent `frontline-p23` run interleaves its own `[exp-offense]`/mod-load lines; attribute by the new `[exp-reach]` format, which only this branch's build emits.)

## 2026-08-03 — The AI has NO terrain/water/bridge/reachability model: POI distance is Euclidean crow-flies, amphibious locomotors are read nowhere, engineer bridge-repair has zero AI callers (research: `WORKSPACE/research/frontline-influence.md`, main @ 595b7002)

> **[rejected: superseded research snapshot. This is the root-cause research (main @ 595b7002) that MOTIVATED the frontline phases; the "AI has NO terrain/water/reachability model" framing is now stale — Phases 0–4 landed (CrossingMap / through-crossing distance / forward staging / frontline profile) and the durable structural facts are banked via the promoted entries above → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging. "Engineer bridge-repair has zero AI callers" stays true but is a dead-end negative not worth banking.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Root-causing the "bot fixates on center bridges, ignores flanks" symptom on River Zeta surfaced a structural blind spot that is the concrete content of the deferred "terrain-aware v2" (`DangerFieldLayer.cs:24-26`). Verified by reading the code:

- **POI attack-axis distance is Euclidean crow-flies from the bot's own SR** — `distCells = (actor.CenterPosition - ownSr.CenterPosition).Length / 1024` (`PoiMap.cs:352-354`), fed into `PoiScoring.DistanceFactor` (`:578-583`). A river between SR and POI does NOT lengthen it. Score is a multiplicative product (`PoiScoring.Score`, `:662-663`), so on a symmetric river map the central bridges (shortest crossing to the far bank) dominate the score, and the top-k axes + score-proportional unit split (`DesiredAxisCount` `:1779`, `AllocateProportional` `:1795`, split `:1829`) funnel the army there. `PoiMap.Discover` (`:203-227`) has NO reachability/path/water check — grep `reachab|PathFinder` in `PoiMap.cs` is empty.
- **Amphibious movement is invisible to AI.** 4 amphibious locomotors with nonzero water speed exist (`world.yaml:43/76/138/179`), bound to IFV/APC actors (`vehicles-russia.yaml:61/174`, `vehicles-america.yaml:222`, `infantry.yaml:2020`). `[Aa]mphibious` matches NOWHERE in `engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/`. Offense issues one **untyped** grouped `AttackMove` to the target (`PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:1277`) with no locomotor/reachability discrimination. The only reachability check in squad AI is naval-only (`NavyStates.cs:36`).
- **Engineer bridge repair works as an engine mechanic but has zero AI callers.** `e6` carries `RepairsBridges` (`infantry.yaml:1903`) → enters `LegacyBridgeHut` (`civilian.yaml:856/867`) via the `"RepairBridge"` order (`RepairsBridges.cs:63/68`). `RepairBridge`/`BridgeHut` appear in no bot module. Bridges/huts are never even discovered as POIs (no income weight, no `CaptureManager`). No route-opening awareness (engineer OR amphibious) exists anywhere — not even dead code.
- **The free pool is a recruitment set, never a move command.** `BuildFreePool` (`PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:1025-1035`) collects idle eligible combat units but the `free` list is only Add/Remove/Count'd — no `QueueOrder` ever targets it. Uncommitted units idle at the SR rally (never advanced; `supply-route.md:105` intent unimplemented). Compounded by the `RetreatWhenLosing` FSM oscillating small `EarlyGameSpread` axes into the 10-cell SR bubble (`MissionCommitmentEnabled` exempts retreating axes). These are the code causes of "units pool/shuffle near spawn."

Implication: the influence stack's fields (danger/control) are radial and terrain-blind by construction; a river-split front, crossings-as-chokepoints, and amphibious-vs-land reachability are all unrepresented. Full gap analysis + phased design (reachability/crossing map → frontline strength profile → man-the-line, all `@experimental`-gated, byte-identical off) in `WORKSPACE/research/frontline-influence.md`.

## 2026-08-03 — transport-heli EMPTY-DELIVERY + littlebird survivability (`auto/heli-fixes`, from main @ 595b7002)

> **[promoted (partial): the EnterTransport EMPTY-DELIVERY boarding gotcha (a queued carrier Move fires immediately on the idle carrier's own queue; poll `Cargo.PassengerCount`; stage a `Loading` task; queue the return Move behind Unload) → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise. Verified `HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:841/:912/:939/:993-1002`. The littlebird-is-Scout / `CleanUpHelicopters`-re-pool / `ReconSafetyMath` details are module-impl, left here.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Two heli-AI fixes in `HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs`. Grounded facts:

- **A bot that orders passengers to `EnterTransport` and queues the carrier's `Move`→`Unload`→`Move` chain in the SAME pass flies the delivery EMPTY.** Root cause of the empty-transport bug: the `EnterTransport` orders land on the *infantry's* activity queues, but the queued `Move` lands on the *transport's* OWN (empty) queue, so `queued:true` on an idle actor starts the Move IMMEDIATELY — the heli departs before any soldier walks over and boards. `HelicopterSquadBotModule.TryLaunchTransportMission` did exactly this (pre-fix `:855-877`). The engine gives no boarding-complete callback; boarding "completes" when `Cargo.Load` fires (`RideTransport.OnEnterComplete`, `Cargo.cs:450`), observable only by polling `Cargo.PassengerCount`. Fix = the proven `MountedTransportBotModule` shape: stage a `Loading` task, dispatch the delivery ONLY once `PassengerCount >= min` (or partial on timeout), ABORT to the idle pool if nobody boarded. Extracted to pure `TransportLoadMath.Decide` (NUnit-pinned). This is a **bug-class / ungated** correctness fix — the staged loading applies to every profile (@stable + @experimental + legacy), because a transport flying empty is wrong for all of them. Builds ON the recently-merged transport-retreat (`transportsAwaitingUnload`/`EnsureTransportsUnload`, e946dfa9): dispatch still hands the loaded heli to that safety net.
- **`CleanUpHelicopters` re-pools ANY managed non-squad heli into `idleHelicopters`.** So a transport mid-load (or mid-delivery) is silently re-added to the idle pool and could be re-picked for a *second* mission. New `Loading` tasks and `transportsAwaitingUnload` members must be explicitly skipped in that re-pool loop. This is why the fix guards both.
- **The littlebird is `AIHelicopterRole: Scout` (not Transport), so it flies the RECON path, and that path had ZERO danger awareness.** `PickReconTarget`/`ConsiderReconCandidate` scored candidates on exploration-staleness + POI + edge only — a believed enemy-SR POI or an edge cell deep in AA scored HIGH, so the fragile scout was routed straight through believed anti-air and shot down. (The HIND is `AttackHeavy` and already gets Stage-D `DangerFieldAvoidance` + `MinFrontierDistanceCells` in @experimental, so it was already covered — the reported "littlebird flies into enemy territory" was the *scout* gap.) Fix = a fog-legal air-danger gate + penetration cap on the recon picker, gated behind default-off `CarefulScoutEmployment` (byte-identical for @stable/legacy). Reads `DangerFieldLayer.AirDanger` (Stage B, reads 0 for unscouted cells) and reuses `HeliDangerNav.PathMaxAirDanger` for route exposure; pure decision in `ReconSafetyMath.Acceptable` (NUnit-pinned). The geometry cap (`ScoutMaxDistanceCells`) is what bounds penetration into *unscouted* territory — belief data can't gate what hasn't been seen, so only distance can; before contact the danger field is empty and the cap does all the work, which is how the "strengthen the first-contact gate" requirement is met.
- **littlebird ($3000, Scout) AND HIND ($4000, AttackHeavy) both carry `Cargo`** but neither is `Role: Transport`, so the AI never loads troops into them — their Cargo is unused by the bot. The user's "primarily a troop carrier" doctrine is about the *airframe*, but the in-code employment lever for the littlebird is its recon path, not a transport path.

## 2026-08-03 — frontline-influence Phases 2+3 shipped (free-pool forward staging + retreat-oscillation damper) — `auto/frontline-p23` from main @ b2054d16

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Frontline reachability & staging (forward staging = steepest descent on `ControlField.FrontierDistanceAt`, not `RearwardSteps`; retreat damper delays only RE-advance, never a withdrawal; the free-pool-drained-to-0 correction). Verified `ForwardStagingMath.cs:88-138`, `RetreatDamperMath.cs:50-62`, `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:363/:399/:721/:1334`. The `--check-yaml` invocation gotcha is AUTOTEST/harness material, not banked.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Implemented the two behavior-wiring fixes for the "units pool near spawn making small movements, clogging the road to the front" symptom. Both `@experimental`-gated default-off; flags off ⇒ every profile byte-identical to main. New pure math `ForwardStagingMath` / `RetreatDamperMath` (nested-style engine-free statics, NUnit-pinned: `ForwardStagingMathTest`, `RetreatDamperTest`). Non-obvious facts for the next reader:

- **The free pool is NOT a standing idle reservoir the way the research read (bullet 13 above) implies — `AllocateProportional` DRAINS it to 0 most evals.** `AllocateProportional` (`PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:~1795`) distributes the ENTIRE `totalOffensive` across the funded ≤`MaxAxes` axes (leftover fully spread by score), and the recruit loop then fills each axis from `free`, so in steady state `free == 0`. Confirmed live: the `test-experimental-poi-harness` run logged `[exp-offense] reeval player=USA-bot … free=0` at EVERY eval (pool 3–20). The idle reservoir Phase 2 targets materialises ONLY when units are WITHHELD from allocation: `NoReinforceLostFights` skipping a losing axis's top-up (`:741 continue`), an under-min axis release (`:857` releases without re-adding to `free`), or a released/retreating batch that no axis's `need` reclaims that eval. So Phase 2's live effect is bounded to those cases — the small-army/short poi-harness scenario never produced a non-empty pool, so it did NOT exercise the staging path live (it PASSED and confirmed integration health + no crash + the Phase-3 retreat FSM firing, but the staging bar needs a scenario that withholds units — large late-game army, or a sustained losing axis). The staging MATH is what the NUnit pins prove; the wiring is exercised each eval (control field resolved, `ResolveStagingAnchor` called) and correctly no-ops at `free==0`.
- **Forward staging uses STEEPEST DESCENT on `ControlField.FrontierDistanceAt`, NOT `FrontierStandoffMath.RearwardSteps`.** `RearwardSteps` walks a point AWAY from a KNOWN target (the echelon anchor pushes back from its axis POI); the free pool is TARGET-LESS, so there is no away-bearing. The frontier-distance BFS gradient is the natural primitive: the SR sits deep in the rear (large distance), each descent step toward a smaller distance steps toward the nearest front, and the walk halts `StagingStandoffCells` short of the line. A FLAT field (no believed enemy ⇒ every cell the `MaxFrontierDistanceCells` sentinel) yields no improving neighbour ⇒ returns the SR ⇒ inert until populated (the byte-identical path). A danger guard (stop before a cell whose `GroundDanger > threshold`) holds the muster BEHIND defended fronts even when the standoff isn't reached — belt-and-suspenders with the standoff floor.
- **The retreat FSM ALREADY had entry hysteresis; the missing anti-oscillation piece was the RE-ADVANCE gate, not entry.** `CombatRetreatMath.Step` already damps ENTRY (a sustained losing STREAK of `RetreatSustainEvals`, plus an asymmetric stricter `ReengageForceRatioPct` exit band) — so Phase-3 item (b) "persist across N evals, not one sample" was already satisfied and I did NOT touch `Step` (keeps the base retreat lever byte-identical). The genuinely-missing pieces were (a) a post-retreat DWELL — after a retreat COMPLETES (Retreating→Engaged at safety), hold `RetreatReadvanceDwellEvals` evals before re-advancing on the same target — and (c) an advance-STRENGTH floor. `RetreatDamperMath.StepReadvanceHold` returns 0 whenever the axis is Retreating, which is the load-bearing safety property: the damper can ONLY delay RE-advance/filter massing, NEVER delay a genuine withdrawal (pinned by the end-to-end sequence test).
- **Damper composes with staging: a dwelling/sub-floor axis holds at the forward staging anchor (`stagingAnchor ?? rallyCell`), off the SR road,** reusing `OrderRetreat`'s gated grouped `AttackMove`. Both the damper-hold and the free-pool stager read one shared `stagingAnchor` resolved once per eval (before `CommitAndOrder`), so they can't disagree on the muster point.
- **`--check-yaml` invocation gotcha (for running it OUTSIDE `make.ps1 test`):** the utility resolves `ENGINE_DIR` relative to the EXE dir (`engine/bin`), so it must be `..` (matching `make.ps1`'s `$env:ENGINE_DIR=".."`), and `MOD_SEARCH_PATHS` must include BOTH `./mods` AND `./engine/mods` or the ww3mod manifest's base-`ra` dependency fails to load (`Could not load mod 'ra'`). The `Errors: N` tally is the known ~422–438 map-cordon baseline (per the 2026-07-30 transport entry) — grep the output for your own keys (`ai.yaml`/new field names); a mistyped YAML key surfaces as a field-not-found error naming it. My run: 438 total, zero referencing any new key.

## 2026-08-03 — behavior-lint FIRST SLICE shipped (`auto/behavior-lint`, from main @ 1c3cb070): UnitLifecycleLogger + analyzer, and the `Game.OnQuit`-vs-teardown gotcha

> **[rejected: diagnostic-tooling / branch narrative. The `UnitLifecycleLogger` + analyzer is a WORKSPACE dev tool (home: `WORKSPACE/behavior-lint-spec.md`), not shipped gameplay. The one broadly-durable engine fact (`Game.Exit` doesn't flush; `OnQuit` fires AFTER `worldRenderer`/`ModData` Dispose so the world is unreadable there) is real but niche end-of-game-hook lore; `InfluenceMap`-allocates-a-grid-per-call is already implied by influence-stack's omniscient-InfluenceMap note. Not reference-bank material.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Implemented the first slice of `WORKSPACE/behavior-lint-spec.md` (meta/spawn/order/idle_start/idle_end/death(minimal)/end + analyzer rules R1/R2/R6/R8). Grounded facts + deviations for the full build:

- **`Game.Exit()` does NOT flush anything and `Game.OnQuit` fires too late to read the world.** `Game.Exit()` (`Game.cs:1101`) merely sets `state = Success`; the game loop then unwinds and `OnQuit()` is invoked at `Game.cs:1096` **after** `worldRenderer.Dispose()` + `ModData.Dispose()`. So the end-of-game census MUST be built from trait-held state only — reading `world.Actors`/`InfluenceMap` at OnQuit is unsafe. Solution: the logger keeps a self-contained `Dictionary<uint,UnitTrack>` and refreshes `LastCell`/idle state every tick, so `Flush()` (hooked on `Game.OnQuit`, guarded by a `flushed` bool + immediate unsubscribe) needs zero world reads. `world.WorldTick` is a plain int auto-property and stays readable post-teardown, so it's used for the final tick.
- **`InfluenceMap.GetEnemyInfluence/GetFriendlyInfluence` allocate a fresh `int[,]` grid on EVERY call** (`InfluenceMap.cs:143/:156`). Attaching `terr` to edge events would allocate a grid per idle edge — cached per `(owner, tick)` in the logger so co-tick edges reuse one pair of grids. Still logging-ON-only cost.
- **Zero-cost-when-off proof:** `UnitLifecycleLogger.WorldLoaded` returns before opening a file / subscribing / hooking `OnQuit` unless `TestMode.IsActive && TestMode.UnitLifecycleLogPath != null`; `enabled` stays false. `ModularBot.QueueOrder` calls `lifecycleLogger?.LogOrder(...)` which early-returns on `!enabled` before any allocation. The `currentModuleTag = t.GetType().Name` set around the tick loops is a cached-string field write (RuntimeType caches `.Name`), so it is allocation-free after first touch even when logging is off.
- **DEVIATION from §2a (minor, additive):** §2a's minimal `death` schema is `{x,y,orders}`, but §2d says terr is attached to death/idle/end. Followed §2d — the `death` line also carries `terr` (omniscient `InfluenceMap` bucket). Harmless superset; the analyzer reads it for the drill-down but no first-slice rule depends on it.
- **DEVIATION from §2b (scope, first slice):** "game active for owner" narrowing by SR-loss is deferred — the first slice has no SR-actor tagging, so R1/R2's "while at war" window is the whole match (min→max event tick). Noted in `behavior_lint.py:match_window`. Full build adds per-side SR-loss from a tagged SR death.
- **Testability:** idle-span arithmetic (fold spans → total + longest; snapshot an open span at match end without mutating) extracted to the pure `IdleSpanAccumulator` struct and pinned in `IdleSpanMathTest.cs` (9 cases: idempotent Start, no-op End, negative-dur clamp, non-mutating Snapshot). Suite 745 → 754, all green.
- **Review polish (R1 false-positive flood):** `IsInteresting` tracks structures too (they carry `UpdatesPlayerStatisticsInfo`; `mods/ww3mod/rules/ingame/structures.yaml:98,213`), so the "forgotten unit" rules would flag every structure + the Supply Route every match. Clean discriminator: `IPositionableInfo` — `BuildingInfo` implements `IOccupySpaceInfo` but NOT `IPositionableInfo` (`Building.cs:29`), while Mobile/Aircraft do. The trait now stamps a `mobile` field on the `spawn` line; the analyzer gates R1/R2/R6 **and** the R8 census on it. R1/R6 also skip units that lived `< --min-life` ticks (default 250) so late call-ins aren't miscounted as forgotten. Structures stay tracked (needed for order-target resolution) but never flagged.

## 2026-08-03 — `ModularBot.QueueOrder` is the single funnel for ALL bot-issued orders; issuing-module identity is recoverable there with no per-call-site edits (spec: `WORKSPACE/behavior-lint-spec.md`, main @ 45210768)

> **[promoted: → architecture.md §All bot orders funnel through `ModularBot.QueueOrder` (single choke point at `:91`; issuing-module identity recoverable via a `currentModuleTag` set around the enabled-only BotTick loop `:111-116`). Verified `ModularBot.cs:91/:97/:111-116/:131/:137`. The omniscient-InfluenceMap-vs-belief-ControlField territory-read distinction is already banked in influence-stack.md/architecture.md.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Researching a unit-lifecycle logger to auto-detect "strange AI behavior" (idling/parked/never-re-tasked units) from sim logs. Key structural facts for any future per-order instrumentation:

- **One choke point.** Every `bot.QueueOrder(...)` call across the ~25 BotModules lands in `ModularBot.QueueOrder(Order)` (`engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ModularBot.cs:81-84`), which enqueues; `ModularBot.Tick` (`:101-112`) dequeues and `world.IssueOrder`s them. Tagging every order with its origin is a single-file change, not 25.
- **Module identity is known at the tick loop, not at `QueueOrder`.** The order carries no producer. But `ModularBot.Tick` runs each `IBotTick` module via `t.BotTick(this)` (`:95-97`) and attack responses via `RespondToAttack` (`:124-126`). Set a `currentModuleTag = t.GetType().Name` field around those two loops and read it in `QueueOrder` → per-order module attribution for free.
- **No bot-order logging exists today.** `PlayerStatistics.ResolveOrder` (`PlayerStatistics.cs:122-128`) only bumps a global `OrderCount` (skips `Dev*`), no per-unit/module/target.
- **Per-unit-type telemetry (verdict_version 7, `UnitTypeTelemetry` in `PlayerStatistics.cs:203-252`) is per-player×per-type AGGREGATE only** — produced/lost/alive counts+cost, no ActorID/position/time/order resolution. Fed by `UpdatesPlayerStatistics` INotify callbacks; serialized as the `unit_types` block (`BotVsBotMatchWatcher.cs:586-611`).
- **Territory classification for an arbitrary bot must use the OMNISCIENT `InfluenceMap`, not the belief `ControlField`.** `ControlField.OwnerAt`/`DangerFieldLayer.GroundDanger` only exist for `InfluenceStack.Participates` players (`@experimental` + humans; `InfluenceStack.cs:38-48`) — `@stable`/normal tournament bots have no field. `InfluenceMap.GetEnemyInfluence/GetFriendlyInfluence` (`InfluenceMap.cs:143/:156`) scan `world.Actors` fog-free for every profile and are legal at LOG time (diagnostics ≠ sim).
- **Off-by-default logging gate idiom:** launch arg via `TestMode` (parse in `TestMode.cs:90-129`, no-op unless `TestMode.IsActive`), writing a sibling of `ResultPath` (`Path.ChangeExtension(...,".jsonl")`) — same pattern as the watcher's `.watcher.log` (`BotVsBotMatchWatcher.cs:146-159`). Global spawn/death hooks: `World.ActorAdded/ActorRemoved` (`World.cs:436-437`); death CAUSE needs `INotifyKilled`'s `AttackInfo` (not on `ActorRemoved`).

## 2026-08-03 — Off-map `Map.GetTerrainInfo(CPos)` CTD family: HuskDecay crash root-caused + guarded, source clamped, one twin found (`auto/husk-crash`, from main @ 45210768)

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise (`Map.GetTerrainInfo(CPos)`/`GetTerrainIndex(CPos)` are unguarded — an off-map cell throws IndexOutOfRange; gate behind `Map.Contains` or `Map.Clamp`; death-effect husks/trails are the recurring off-map source). Verified `Map.cs:1363/:1627/:1637/:1649/:1654`. The per-file HuskDecay/LeavesTrailsCA fix sites are the commit's job, not reference.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Recurring hard crash `IndexOutOfRangeException` at `Map.GetTerrainIndex` (`Map.cs:1630`) from `HuskDecay.AddedToWorld` (`HuskDecay.cs:70`). Root-caused, fixed at source + consumer, swept the whole `GetTerrainInfo(CPos)`/`GetTerrainIndex(CPos)` surface for the same class.

- **Root cause chain (aircraft-over-edge → off-map husk):** an aircraft dies → `SpawnActorOnDeath` spawns a *flying* husk (e.g. `HELI.Husk.moving`) with `FallsToEarth: Moves: True` → the `FallToEarth` activity (`Activities/Air/FallToEarth.cs:57-59`) drives it forward with `aircraft.SetPosition` and **no bounds check**, so a husk crashing near the map edge can drift PAST it → on touchdown it kills itself → `SpawnActorOnDeath.RemovedFromWorld` spawns the *ground* husk at the off-map `self.Location` → the ground husk's `HuskDecay.AddedToWorld` calls `Map.GetTerrainInfo(self.Location)` → `GetTerrainIndex` indexes the per-cell `cachedTerrainIndexes[uv]` array unguarded → IndexOutOfRange CTD.
- **Why `GetTerrainInfo(CPos)` is the sharp edge:** it delegates to `GetTerrainIndex(cell)` which does `cachedTerrainIndexes[cell.ToMPos(this)]` — a raw `CellLayer` array index with no `Contains` guard (`Map.cs:1636-1637`). The engine idiom everywhere else is to gate it behind `Map.Contains(cell)` first (Aircraft `CanEnterCell`/`CanLand`, Wanders, Husk `CanExistInCell`, Missile `:1053` with an explicit "avoids IndexOutOfRange" comment, HeliEmergencyLanding, LayeredDefenceBotModule, AIUtils). HuskDecay was the one consumer that read it unguarded.
- **Fix (source AND consumer, per belt-and-braces):** (1) **`HuskDecay.cs:68-78`** — guard the lookup: `onWater = map.Contains(loc) && WaterTerrainTypes.Contains(...)`; off-map defaults to land decay (fade + dispose). This is the robust catch-all — it protects against ANY path that adds a husk off-map, not just this one. (2) **`SpawnActorOnDeath.cs:116`** — clamp the source: when `!map.Contains(self.Location + Offset)`, `Map.Clamp` the cell into bounds and snap `CenterPositionInit` to `CenterOfCell(clamped)+Z` so the two inits stay consistent. In-bounds deaths are byte-identical (guard is a no-op).
- **SWEEP — one genuine twin found and fixed:** **`LeavesTrailsCA.cs:125`** had its `if (!Contains(spawnCell)) return;` guard *deliberately commented out* ("removed for CA version for V3/ICBM") but still called `GetTerrainInfo(spawnCell)` unguarded. Ballistic-missile trails (`vehicles-russia.yaml:1040`, an arc/terminal-dive BM; `vehicles-america.yaml:1118`) can have their `CenterPosition` off-map at the edge → same CTD. Fixed to preserve the CA intent: read terrain only in-bounds; off-map, untyped trails (`TerrainTypes` empty — the V3/ICBM case) still spawn, terrain-restricted trails skip (can never match off-map terrain anyway). The subtle decision is extracted to `LeavesTrailsCAMath.SkipsOffMapTrail(inBounds, restrictionCount)` and pinned.
- **SWEEP — surveyed and LEFT (with reason):** every other `GetTerrainInfo(CPos)`/`GetTerrainIndex(CPos)` call in `OpenRA.Mods.Common` is either (a) already `Contains`-guarded (the list above), (b) reads `self.Location`/`self.CenterPosition` of an actor already in-world / a viewport-clamped cursor cell (in-bounds by construction: Cargo, DamagedByTerrain, WithCrateBody, GrantConditionOnDeploy/Terrain, TransformsIntoMobile, Mobile, Parachutable), (c) iterates in-bounds map cells or layer init (Resource/Editor/Jumpjet/Subterranean/Bridge layers), or (d) takes the `Rules.TerrainInfo.GetTerrainIndex(string/TerrainTile)` overload, which does NOT index a per-cell array and cannot throw off-map. The stock warhead-impact reads (`CreateEffectWarhead:156`, `WarheadAS:67`, `LeaveSmudgeWarhead:59`, `Bullet:324`) are upstream `release-20230225`, not WW3MOD-modified, and resolve against in-bounds targets — left as upstream scope.
- **Coverage:** new `LeavesTrailsCAMathTest` (3 pins: in-bounds never skips; off-map unrestricted spawns; off-map restricted skips). Suite **745/745** (742 baseline + 3). `./make.ps1 all` 0 errors. HuskDecay/SpawnActorOnDeath guards are world-touching (delegate to well-tested `Map.Contains`/`Map.Clamp`) so not separately unit-pinned.

## 2026-08-03 — Scout-heli (littlebird) corner-park ROOT CAUSE: the heli scout path reads exploration-age but never writes it, so `GetExplorationAge` is `int.MaxValue` everywhere and the picker locks onto a fixed map corner forever (`auto/littlebird-missions`, from main @ 45210768)

> **[rejected: fixed-bug narrative. The littlebird corner-park is a fixed defect (the fix is in code + the commit message); `GetExplorationAge == int.MaxValue`-for-unvisited and "the heli scout path must `MarkExplored`" are scout-impl details, not durable general reference. The facts verify (`ThreatMapManager.cs:325/:333`) but don't earn a reference-bank home.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

The user's "both bot profiles send littlebirds to one corner and never re-task them" is a degenerate-target bug in `HelicopterSquadBotModule.TryLaunchScoutMission`, not a unit-config or exclusion problem. Full fix + report on the branch.

- **The littlebird is NOT excluded from the heli system — it has `AIHelicopterRole: Role: Scout`** (`mods/ww3mod/rules/ingame/aircraft-america.yaml:109`), so `FindNewHelicopters` adopts it and the scout path owns it. The hypothesis "littlebirds fall through to legacy scout logic" is wrong; the heli scout logic itself is the defect.
- **Root cause (two facts compounding):** (1) `ThreatMapManager.GetExplorationAge` returns `int.MaxValue` for every never-visited grid cell (`lastExploredTick == 0`, `ThreatMapManager.cs:333-341`). (2) The heli scout path read that value but **NEVER called `MarkExplored`** — only the ground `ScoutBotModule` does (`ScoutBotModule.cs:110` scout position, `:131` target). So the age grid stays `int.MaxValue` almost everywhere, and the old picker's strict `age > bestAge` from `bestAge = 0` locks onto the **first in-bounds grid cell** — a fixed map corner via `GridToMapCell(gx,gy) = (gx*8+4, gy*8+4)` iterated `gx` outer, `gy` inner. Every `ScoutInterval` (400t) the littlebird is re-issued a `Move` to the identical corner it already sits on ⇒ looks like it never moves again. Shared code, no gate ⇒ BOTH `@stable` and `@experimental` exhibit it (same class as the earlier AirUnitsTypes both-profiles case fix).
- **Also:** the old picker tasked only ONE scout (`.FirstOrDefault()`), so a second littlebird piled onto the same corner; and the scout dispatch sat behind `activeSquads.Count >= MaxActiveSquads` even though scouts never form a squad — 3 live attack/transport squads silently benched all recon.
- **Fix:** mark the shared exploration grid from scout-heli positions each scan (mirror `ScoutBotModule`), task EVERY idle scout to a DISTINCT rotating destination (believed POI via `PoiMap.GetOffensiveTargets(..., suppressOmniscientThreat:true)` or stalest far area), mark the destination explored on dispatch, and score with a bounded/overflow-safe `ScoutReconMath.Score` (POI > edge > staleness, far-first distance tie-break) so the sweep spreads from the opening instead of camping a corner. Zero RNG, deterministic.
- **Coupling note (review N1):** heli scouts now WRITE the shared world-level exploration grid, so @stable ground `ScoutBotModule` target selection is coupled to heli recon (shared "where have we looked" staleness). Benign and in-scope, but a real cross-module side effect.
- **AIR-ASSAULT POTENTIAL (logged, NOT built this branch):** the littlebird carries `Cargo: Types: Infantry, MaxWeight: 4` (`aircraft-america.yaml:222-227`) — it is a troop-capable scout. A future feature could give the `@experimental` bot a light air-assault employment (load 4 infantry near the SR, insert onto a lightly-defended POI or flank behind the believed front) reusing the transport heli's `EnterTransport`/`Move`/`Unload` order pattern and the belief/danger fields for a fog-legal safe LZ pick. Out of scope here (this branch delivers purposeful recon only); worth a design pass.

## 2026-08-03 — "Orderless-at-hostile-location" is a bot bug CLASS; only DEDICATED (free-pool-excluded) units leak — combat units self-heal (`auto/transport-retreat`)

> **[promoted: → architecture.md §The bot free pool self-heals — only free-pool-EXCLUDED units can leak (idle `AttackBase` combat units re-collected by `BuildFreePool`'s global `world.Actors` scan regardless of location; only CaptureSpecialist/Logistics/Recon/TransportLift/ShortRangeAD/TroopCarrier leak). Verified `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:1316-1326/:1439/:1455-1460`, `UnitRoleResolver.cs:37-48/:239`.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

User watched a transport heli fly infantry to a drop point, unload, then sit IDLE at the drop deep in contested territory — a free kill. Root-caused + fixed the class, not just the instance.

- **The observed unit is NOT owned by `MountedTransportBotModule`.** That module's `CarrierTypes` are GROUND vehicles (`bradley,bmp2,m113`); transport HELICOPTERS are driven by `HelicopterSquadBotModule.TryLaunchTransportMission` (`HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:556`). Its order sequence was `EnterTransport… → Move(dropZone) → Unload` and then NOTHING — so on unload the heli's activity queue empties and it idles at the drop. Nothing re-collects it: `EvaluateIdleHelicopters` only acts on `AttackHeavy/AttackLight` roles (`:709`), never `Transport`; `CleanUpHelicopters` only re-pools it for the NEXT transport mission (≥4 idle infantry + a weak drop cell, up to `TransportInterval`=600t away). FIX: queue a `Move` back to the own SR right behind the `Unload` (`:623`). Ungated bug fix ⇒ applies to every profile running the module (`@stable`+`@experimental`; heli transport is NOT in Normal/Rush/Turtle — `enable-ai-any` = stable+experimental only).
- **`MountedTransportBotModule` already retreated — but with a scan-gap.** Its `Unloading` state issues the return `Move` only once it DETECTS empty cargo (`:438`), i.e. up to a full `ScanInterval` (50t) after unload — an idle window at the drop. FIX: pre-queue the return `Move` (queued=true) right behind the `Unload`, gated on `UnloadOnArrival && cargo.CanUnload()` so (a) it's inert/byte-identical for a twin with the frozen `UnloadCargo` no-op or no free cell, and (b) a dropped `Unload` can't fly the carrier home still loaded. The empty-detection path is untouched, so ledger-release + capture-ferry hand-back still run.
- **The self-healing invariant (why most idle units are FINE).** Idle COMBAT units are re-collected regardless of location: `PoiOffensiveBotModule.BuildFreePool` (`:1025`) scans ALL `world.Actors` filtered by `IsEligibleCombatUnit` (requires `AttackBase`), and Garrison/LaneAmbush/LayeredDefence/SquadManager use the same global scan. So leaving a weapon-bearing unit idle anywhere is self-healing — NOT a leak. Only classes EXCLUDED from that pool can leak: `CaptureSpecialist`, `Logistics`, `Recon`, `TransportLift`, `ShortRangeAD` (`UnitRoleResolver`).
- **The one other genuine leak found: post-capture TECN.** `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.ReconcileGuardCommitments` releases the ledger on capture-complete/target-gone (`:1105`) but issued NO follow-up order — a `CaptureSpecialist` (no `AttackBase`) is excluded from every free pool AND this module's own escort/defender recruitment (`!CapturerNames.Contains`), so nothing brought a surviving TECN home. FIX: new `RetreatCapturerWhenDone` flag (default false, engine class byte-identical) → queue a `Move` to the own SR on release; enabled on both live `.tecn` twins. `test-experimental-poi-capture` still passes (capture completes before the retreat fires).
- **Found-FINE, documented not changed:** escorts/defenders/garrison/ambush (all `AttackBase` combat ⇒ re-collected); scouts (job never "completes" — continuously re-tasked by design). Minor edge (not a job-completion leak): `SupplyFollowerBotModule` when `clusters.Count==0` leaves a full forward truck orderless until a danger-evac or restock trigger fires.

## 2026-08-02 — Case-mismatch defect family HARDENED at the engine level: one lowercase-normalize helper wired into every bot-module actor-name config field (`auto/case-hardening`)

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise (the actor-name case-mismatch pitfall + the `ActorNameCase` engine-level hardening + why-not-`OrdinalIgnoreCase`). Verified `ActorNameCase.cs:37/:51`, `FieldLoader.cs:506/:524`, `GameRules/Ruleset.cs:126`. Merged with the 2026-08-02 minefield-audit entry below.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Durable fix for the minefield the same-day audit below documented. Closes the 2 confirmed defects at the mechanism level (not just their YAML) and disarms all latent + half-guarded + inert-latent fields, so a future uppercase config typo can never again silently no-match.

- **Mechanism chosen: lowercase-normalize the collection contents once at load, in each Info's `RulesetLoaded`.** New helper `ActorNameCase` (`engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/BotModules/ActorNameCase.cs`): `NormalizeInPlace(HashSet<string>)` and `NormalizeKeysInPlace(Dictionary<string,int>)`, both mutating the existing (readonly-held) collection in place (Clear + re-add lowercased) and idempotent.
- **Why NOT `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`.** `FieldLoader.ParseHashSetOrList`/`ParseDictionary` (`engine/OpenRA.Game/FieldLoader.cs:500-536`) build each collection with `Activator.CreateInstance(fieldType, capacity)` — a fresh DEFAULT-comparer instance that discards any comparer set in the field initializer. To swap the comparer you must REPLACE the instance, but these fields are `readonly` (can't reassign without reflection or dropping readonly). Lowercasing the contents needs no reassignment, touches only the flagged collections, and cannot regress ordinal semantics for any other string set (production-queue `Type` sets, target-type `BitSet`s, terrain/cohesion enums stay ordinal).
- **Behavior-identity (both @stable and @experimental, today).** Every flagged field's current YAML values in `mods/ww3mod/rules/ai/{ai,ai-america,ai-russia}.yaml` are all-lowercase (verified field-by-field), so `ToLowerInvariant()` maps each to itself and the normalized collection is element-identical. Consumers compare against always-lowercase actor names (`Ruleset.cs:126`), so all matches are unchanged. The ONLY behavior that changes is a future uppercase value: silent miss → still matches.
- **Fields hardened (RulesetLoaded call site → normalized fields):** `SquadManagerBotModule.cs:107` (AirUnitsTypes, ExcludeFromSquadsTypes, NavalUnitsTypes, IncludeInSquadTypes, ConstructionYardTypes, NavalProductionTypes, ProtectionTypes); `UnitBuilderBotModule.cs:75` (UnitsToBuild, UnitLimits, UnitDelays, ResupplyUnitTypes, AntiAirUnitTypes); `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.cs:246` (CapturingActorTypes, CapturableActorTypes [half-guarded], SupportingUnitTypes, IncomeWeights); `BaseBuilderBotModule.cs:106` (ConstructionYardTypes, VehiclesFactoryTypes, BarracksTypes, HeliTypes, AirfieldTypes, ProductionTypes, NavalProductionTypes, DefenseTypes, BuildingFractions, BuildingLimits, BuildingDelays); `AdaptiveProductionBotModule.cs:142` (AntiVehicleUnits, AntiInfantryUnits, AntiAirUnits, AirStrikeUnits); `PoiOffensiveBotModule.cs:392`/`PoiGarrisonBotModule.cs:129`/`LaneAmbushBotModule.cs:110` (ExcludeUnitTypes); `LayeredDefenceBotModule.cs:132` (ScreenUnitTypes, MainLineUnitTypes, ExcludedActorTypes); `SupplyFollowerBotModule.cs:97` (SupplyTruckTypes); `ScoutBotModule.cs:38` (ScoutTypes); `MountedTransportBotModule.cs:117` (CarrierTypes, PassengerTypes [half-guarded]); `GarrisonBotModule.cs:36` (GarrisonActorTypes); `CaptureManagerBotModule.cs:44` (CapturingActorTypes, CapturableActorTypes — legacy, not instantiated, hardened for family completeness).
- **Deliberately LEFT ordinal (would BREAK if lowercased — different namespace, correctly case-sensitive):** production-queue `Type` sets `UnitQueues`/`BuildingQueues`/`DefenseQueues` (`Vehicle`/`Infantry`/`Aircraft`/`Building`/`Defense`); `SquadManager.IgnoredEnemyTargetTypes` (`BitSet<TargetableType>`, tokens `Submarine`/`IgnoreThis`); terrain sets `WaterTerrainTypes`/`CoverTerrainTypes` (`Water`/`Tree`/`Rough`/`Field`); cohesion enums; and the hardcoded lowercase-default `SupplyRouteTypes = {"supplyroute"}` (not user config) across 5 modules.
- **Out of scope (same hazard shape, different trait — NOT a bot module, so outside the audit's boundary): `PoiMap.IncomeWeights`** (`engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/PoiMap.cs:93`, consumed `:212/:348/:415/:483` by `ContainsKey(name)`/`TryGetValue(name)` against actor names; a World trait). Currently lowercase-safe (`world.yaml:309`). Recommended for the same one-line treatment in a follow-up.
- **Coverage:** NUnit `ActorNameCaseTest` (`engine/OpenRA.Test/OpenRA.Mods.Common/ActorNameCaseTest.cs`) pins both mechanisms (uppercase HashSet value + uppercase Dictionary key match a lowercase lookup post-normalize), the behavior-identity/idempotency no-op on all-lowercase input, and null/empty safety. Suite 725/725 (721 baseline + 4 pins). Build clean (`./make.ps1 all`).

## 2026-08-02 — Bot-module actor-name config is a case-mismatch MINEFIELD: 2 confirmed defects (fixed) + ~29 active LATENT fields, all riding one root (`Ruleset.cs:126` lowercases every actor name at load)

> **[promoted (root fact) → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise (same actor-name case pitfall — `GameRules/Ruleset.cs:126` lowercases every actor name, so a case-sensitive config set silently no-matches; the grep tell). The exhaustive latent-field enumeration is superseded by the `ActorNameCase` hardening (entry above) and is ephemeral audit detail, not banked.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Systematic sweep of every bot-module config field in `mods/ww3mod/rules/ai/{ai,ai-america,ai-russia}.yaml` that carries actor-name keys/lists, cross-read against the engine comparison site (not the field name/comment). Static analysis only, no run. Full per-defect evidence + blast radius in [`bugs/discovered.md`](bugs/discovered.md) (2026-08-02 entries).

- **The root cause is ONE fact.** `Ruleset.cs:126` builds every `ActorInfo` with `k.Key.ToLowerInvariant()`, so `actor.Info.Name` is ALWAYS lowercase at runtime. Any bot-module field that stores YAML verbatim in a default `HashSet<string>`/`Dictionary<string,int>` (ordinal, case-SENSITIVE) and then does `Contains(a.Info.Name)` / `ContainsKey(name)` / `b.Name == key` silently NO-MATCHES the moment the YAML value carries an uppercase letter. No warning, no exception — the unit is just never built / never classified / mispriced. **The tell** (grep signature): `= new HashSet<string>()` or `= null` (`Dictionary`) with NO `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`, consumed by `.Contains(<name>)` / `.ContainsKey(<name>)` / `== <key>`.
- **2 CONFIRMED (both fixed this pass, keys lowercased):** (1) `UnitBuilderBotModule` `UnitsToBuild`/`UnitLimits`/`UnitDelays` — `Dictionary<string,int>` (`:31/:34/:37`), compared at `:327` (`b.Name == unit.Key`), `:191/:195/:200` (`ContainsKey`). UPPERCASE `A10/F16/MIG/FROG/HELI/TRAN/HIND/MI28/HALO` → those aircraft UNBUILDABLE for ALL fog bots (`enable-ai-any`: `@experimental` + `@stable`), both factions. Was the "US only ever buys the littlebird" report. (2) `SquadManagerBotModule.AirUnitsTypes` — case-sensitive `HashSet` (`:31`), read at `:351` (classification, now cured by `UseUnitRoles`) AND UNCONDITIONALLY at `:421/:430` (rush own/enemy-aircraft filters, NOT covered by the role gate). UPPERCASE → own aircraft scooped into ground rushes + AI rushes enemy planes.
- **~29 ACTIVE LATENT fields — case-sensitive, currently lowercase-SAFE, one uppercase edit from silent failure.** All below are set in the ww3 YAML with all-lowercase values today, so they work — but they carry ZERO defense against a future uppercase typo. Highest-severity sub-class is the **`Dictionary`-keyed** ones (silent MISPRICE/skip, exactly the confirmed-#1 mechanism): `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.IncomeWeights` (`:57`, looked up at `:1112` with a lowercased name `:1111` — an uppercase key silently falls to `DefaultIncomeWeight`=10, a capture-priority MISPRICE, not a hard fail), `BaseBuilderBotModule.BuildingLimits` (`:101`, `ContainsKey` at `:202/:268`) and `BuildingFractions` (`:98`). **`HashSet`-Contains** latent fields: `CaptureCoordinator.CapturingActorTypes` (`:35`→`:1282/:1319/:1360`); `BaseBuilder` `ConstructionYardTypes`/`VehiclesFactoryTypes`/`BarracksTypes`/`HeliTypes`/`AirfieldTypes`/`ProductionTypes` (`:22-33`→`:115`, `BaseBuilderQueueManager.cs:199`) + `DefenseTypes` (`:39`→`QueueManager:149`); `AdaptiveProductionBotModule` `AntiVehicleUnits`/`AntiInfantryUnits`/`AntiAirUnits`/`AirStrikeUnits` (`:30-111`→`:579`); `UnitBuilder` `ResupplyUnitTypes`/`AntiAirUnitTypes` (`:53/:67`→`:206/:209/:245`); `SquadManager.ExcludeFromSquadsTypes` (`:34`→`:298/:421/:430`); `PoiOffensiveBotModule.ExcludeUnitTypes` (`:100`→`:1056`); `PoiGarrisonBotModule.ExcludeUnitTypes` (`:89`→`:426`); `LaneAmbushBotModule.ExcludeUnitTypes` (`:104`→`:544`); `LayeredDefenceBotModule` `ScreenUnitTypes`/`MainLineUnitTypes`/`ExcludedActorTypes` (`:52/:56/:90`→`:297/:302/:305/:306`); `SupplyFollowerBotModule.SupplyTruckTypes` (`:25`→`:190/:200`); `ScoutBotModule.ScoutTypes` (`:24`→`:135` via `==`).
- **"Half-guarded" latent — `ToLowerInvariant` on the NAME, but the SET is still case-sensitive.** `CaptureCoordinator.CapturableActorTypes` (`:540/:816/:1247` do `Contains(actor.Info.Name.ToLowerInvariant())`) and `MountedTransportBotModule.CarrierTypes`/`PassengerTypes` (`:188/:413/:466`) lowercase the incoming name — but the HashSet is built from raw YAML, so an uppercase YAML VALUE (e.g. `Bradley`) still misses. The `.ToLowerInvariant()` only defends against a hypothetical un-lowercased actor def; the real requirement remains "YAML values must be lowercase." Same latent risk class, NOT immune.
- **INERT-latent (case-sensitive but the field is UNSET in ww3 YAML today):** `SquadManager` `NavalUnitsTypes`/`ProtectionTypes`/`ConstructionYardTypes`/`IncludeInSquadTypes`, `GarrisonBotModule.GarrisonActorTypes`, and the whole legacy `CaptureManagerBotModule` (not instantiated — `@experimental` folded its role into `CaptureCoordinator`). No live risk, but they'd bite if configured with uppercase later.
- **CLEAN — different namespace, correctly case-sensitive, MUST NOT be lowercased.** These look like the family but compare against engine tokens that are NOT lowercased at load, so their capitalization is CORRECT and a naive "lowercase all AI YAML" fix would BREAK them: production-queue `Type` sets `UnitQueues`/`BuildingQueues`/`DefenseQueues` (`Vehicle`/`Infantry`/`Aircraft`/`Building`/`Defense`); `SquadManager.IgnoredEnemyTargetTypes` (target-type tokens `Submarine`/`IgnoreThis`, matched vs `Targetable.TargetTypes`); cohesion enums `ApproachCohesion`/`AssaultCohesion` (`Spread`/`Tight`); terrain sets `CoverTerrainTypes`/`WaterTerrainTypes` (`Tree`/`Rough`/`Field`/`Water`); and the hardcoded-default `SupplyRouteTypes = {"supplyroute"}` (lowercase, not user config) across 5 modules.
- **DURABLE FIX (deferred to the separate reviewed batch, NOT done here).** Per-field lowercasing (what the two confirmed fixes did) is a whack-a-mole that leaves ~29 landmines armed. The real fix is to construct each actor-name `HashSet`/`Dictionary` with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase` at the trait level (`AirUnitsTypes`, the three `UnitBuilder` dicts, `IncomeWeights`, the `BaseBuilder` sets/dicts, `Adaptive*` pools, the `Exclude*`/`*UnitTypes` sets, etc.) so config case can NEVER silently no-op — while explicitly LEAVING the "clean" namespace fields above ordinal. That is an engine change touching `@stable` code paths, so it needs the reviewed-batch + benchmark gate.

## 2026-08-02 — Squad-Brain Phase 4 (strategic-target pinning) landed on `auto/brain-phase4` (from main @ 1c1469a8): the heli FSM's `TargetActor` is BOTH the strategic and the tactical target, so a NEW per-Squad pin field splits them without the (unmerged) Phase-2 Mission object. Key trap: a naive pin loops the FSM forever unless the stall/too-hot transitions RELEASE it.

> **[rejected: branch/design-doc narrative. Squad-Brain Phase 4 strategic-target pinning is implementation of `plans/260802_squad_brain_design.md` §3.3; its home is that design doc. The one general fact (`Squad.StrategicTarget` is transient bot state, not serialized — like `ApproachWaypoint`) is minor and already the documented pattern.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Implements the strategic-target-pinning slice of Phase 4 from [`plans/260802_squad_brain_design.md`](plans/260802_squad_brain_design.md) §3.3/§1.3. Pure-math + FSM wiring + NUnit only; no game run (unit-test scope). Files: `Squad.cs` (two pin fields), `HelicopterStates.cs` (base-state helpers + `HeliMissionPinMath` + 5 FSM integration points), `HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs` (2 Info fields), `ai.yaml` @experimental heli block, `HeliMissionPinMathTest.cs`.

- **The heli squad has NO Mission object to pin to — Phase 2 is unmerged (parallel branch), so the pin lives on `Squad` directly.** Root cause C (§1.3) is that `Squad.TargetActor` is simultaneously the strategic and the micro target, so 5-tick predicate flapping IS strategic churn. The fix adds `Squad.StrategicTarget` (+ `StrategicCommitTick`) as the durable strategic objective, kept separate from the tactical `TargetActor`; the FSM re-aims `TargetActor` on every micro-transition but only the abort triggers touch the pin. This is the heli-squad analogue of `Mission.Objective` and migrates into `SquadBrainBotModule` when Phase 2 lands. **The pin is NOT serialized** — like the pre-existing `Squad.ApproachWaypoint` (`Squad.cs:36`), it is transient bot state, so the save format is byte-identical and a loaded squad resumes unpinned and re-acquires.
- **TRAP — a naive pin makes the FSM loop forever.** The existing `HelicopterApproachState` safeties (`stuckTicks > 200 → Idle` `:614`, and too-hot-no-soft `→ Withdraw`) hand back to a state that, WITH a pin, re-resumes the SAME objective (Idle now routes to the pin instead of re-picking, `:374`). An unreachable / unassailable objective would then cycle Approach→Idle→Approach or Approach→Withdraw→Approach indefinitely. So the pin MUST be released at exactly those two transitions: trigger 6 clears it inside the `stuckTicks > 200` block (`:621`), trigger 2 (N5) clears it in the too-hot-no-soft `else` when the too-hot target IS the objective (`:506-509`, `ReferenceEquals(TargetActor, StrategicTarget)`). Missing either re-introduces the very dither the pin removes, one level up.
- **The heli FSM can feed only a SUBSET of the §3.3 abort triggers — the rest need the Brain.** Pinned-lease check `HeliMissionPinMath.EvaluatePin` (`:880`) covers trigger 1 (objective invalid — a live-actor validity read mirroring `FindClosestEnemy`'s filter, `StrategicTargetValid` `:198`) + the bounded-window backstop; `ObjectiveTooHotAbort` (`:896`) covers the heli form of trigger 2 (objective-itself-too-hot-no-divert, §3.3 N5) reusing the FSM's existing `IsTargetTooHot`; trigger 6 (stall) reuses the FSM's existing `stuckTicks`. Route-danger-spike (full trigger 2) and better-opportunity (trigger 3) need the `DangerFieldLayer` route sample and rival scores — deliberately deferred to `SquadBrainBotModule`, not bolted onto this executor-local pin.
- **Byte-identity: only the flag-OFF path is constrained, and it is trivially unchanged.** Every pin read/write is guarded by `StrategicTargetPinningEnabled(owner)` (`:180`, an Info-bool lookup mirroring `StandoffEngagementEnabled`); with it false, `Squad.StrategicTarget` is never written and each state's target logic collapses to the frozen expression. The flag is set ONLY in `HelicopterSquadBotModule@experimental` (`ai.yaml`); `@stable` OMITS it and takes the engine default `false` — the SAME "parity copy but the mission-commitment experimental flags are deliberately not copied" pattern the offense module's `MissionCommitmentEnabled` uses (`@stable` block `ai.yaml:1028-1068` has no such field). Per-profile trait instance ⇒ the single default-off flag suffices (influence-stack gating pattern 1); no `Participates`-gate needed since this is not a shared-module consumer.
- **Tick source:** `Squad.World` is `internal`, `World.WorldTick` is `public` (`World.cs:442`) — the state classes are same-assembly/same-namespace so `owner.World.WorldTick` is the deterministic commit-tick stamp; no RNG anywhere in the pin path. NUnit **731/731** (721 baseline + 10 pins). `./make.ps1 all` 0 errors.

## 2026-08-02 — Squad-Brain Phase 2 executor commit-on-order audit landed on `auto/brain-phase2` (from main @ 1bae9628): the four known ledger-blind support/passenger/garrison/line writers now commit every unit they order. Key finding: the doc's fifth item — "BuildFreePool ignoring IsPassengerReserved" — needs NO BuildFreePool edit; it is SUBSUMED by the MountedTransport commit-on-load (BuildFreePool already excludes ledger-committed units).

> **[promoted (core invariant) → architecture.md §The PoiGoalGuard commitment ledger (commit-on-order is a PAIR: commit every ordered unit AND recruit only from the ledger-checked pool, else a poach; disjoint objective-key grammar). Verified `PoiGoalGuard.cs:285-300` + the key prefixes across the writer modules. The per-writer audit findings are branch detail whose home is the design doc.]** (curation 2026-08-03).

Implements the §4 / Phase-2 executor-by-executor commit audit from [`plans/260802_squad_brain_design.md`](plans/260802_squad_brain_design.md) (the audit slice only — NOT the `Mission`/`SquadBrainBotModule` objects). Commit-on-order is the coexistence invariant (§4 FIX 3): every executor commits every unit it orders, at order time, AND recruits only from the ledger-checked free pool — both halves are required, since commit-without-recruit-check still lets a writer poach a unit another already committed (see the follow-up MountedTransport fixes below). Pure-math + wiring + NUnit only; no game/autotest run. Files: `PoiGoalGuard.cs` (new `CommitOnOrderMath`), `CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.cs`, `MountedTransportBotModule.cs`, `GarrisonBotModule.cs`, `LayeredDefenceBotModule.cs`, `ai.yaml` (@experimental / shared blocks only), new `CommitOnOrderMathTest.cs`.

- **The ledger runs for BOTH fog-legal bots, so a bare "does the ledger exist" gate is INSUFFICIENT.** `PoiGoalGuard@poi` is gated `enable-ai-experimental || enable-ai-stable` (`ai.yaml:84`) — the @stable bot carries the ledger too (post stable-0802). So committing whenever `goalGuard != null` would change @stable behaviour (its recruitment pool shrinks). Every commit is therefore behind a **default-off per-module flag, set true ONLY in the @experimental block**, mirroring the landed `RespectCommitmentLedger`/`MissionCommitmentEnabled` pattern. Because the ledger itself is @experimental/@stable-gated and every touched writer is a per-profile twin (except Garrison, below), the flag needs NO new `!enable-ai-experimental` clause and NO new YAML on any @stable twin. The gate seam is the new pure `CommitOnOrderMath.ShouldCommit(flag, ledgerAvailable)` (`PoiGoalGuard.cs:292`).
- **AUDIT FINDING 1 — CaptureCoordinator escorts + defenders (CONFIRMED uncommitted, now fixed).** `IssueCaptureOrder` commits only the capturer (`CaptureCoordinatorBotModule.cs:986`). `DispatchEscort` recruits from the ledger-checked pool (`FindIdleSupportersNear` checks `IsCommitted` `:1322`), issues the grouped `AttackMove` (`:1196`), adds to `alreadyRecruited` (`:1198`) — but never committed. `QueueDefenseOrders` recruits defenders, orders them (`:1293`), stamps a **bespoke `defenderBookings` dict** (`:1294-95`) that only THIS module honours — invisible to offense/LayeredDefence.
