**Fix:** treat a squeeze as immovable at `:297` (`squeeze || !mobile.CanEnterCell(...)`). Termination is then two ticks: `EvalPath(Immovable)` returns empty, `Tick` sets `destination = mobile.ToCell` and returns false (`:174-176`), and the next tick hits `destination == mobile.ToCell` and returns true (`:163-164`).

**The trap for the next person:** the branch already stated the correct principle one file away — `Mobile.GetAdjacentCell` carries "a squeeze is geometry, and no amount of the occupant moving widens a corner" — and still missed applying it here, because `Move.cs`'s blocked-handling reads as being about *actors* and a geometric rule does not look like it belongs. It does. The tell for this whole class: a step-legality rule that consults any cell other than the destination.

**Why the autotest did not catch it:** the scenario's `Squeezer` starts far enough away that its `BlockedByActor.None` path runs *through* a trap cell, which trips the `:297` escape by the ordinary `CanEnterCell` route and terminates cleanly. The lane passes for a reason unrelated to the loop — a good reminder that a green behavioural test pins the outcome it asserts, not the mechanism you believe produces it.

## 2026-08-09 — "a host is named" is not "a host exists": the aircraft readiness gates were asking the rules a question only the world can answer

Found while verifying `DOCS/bots/06-inherited-misfits.md` rank 2. The audit's headline held, but its shorthand was wrong twice, and both corrections matter more than the headline.

**Correction 1 — the mechanism is not a disabled trait.** `HPAD` and `AFLD` carry `Buildable.Prerequisites: ~disabled` (`structures.yaml:432`, `:500`), an unsatisfiable *build* prerequisite — **nothing anywhere in the repo provides `disabled`** (verified by grep over `mods/`). The actor definitions are complete and every trait on them is live. They simply can never be instantiated: unbuildable, and pre-placed on **zero** of the ten shipped maps. `LOGISTICSCENTER` is the same (`structures.yaml:367`), which also makes "until the player builds more LCs" in `economy.md` wrong — LCs enter a match only as the Neutral pre-placed capturable ones.

**Correction 2 — "the mod has no rearm" is false, and that is the useful part.** `logisticscenter` has both `RepairsUnits` (`structures.yaml:377`) and `SupplyProvider` (`:387`) and **is pre-placed as a Neutral capturable on three maps** (`polar-disorder-ww3/map.yaml:863,866`; `river-zeta-ww3:3994`, `:9088`; `woodland-warfare-ww3:3695,3698`). Every infantry template names it (`RearmActors: truk, logisticscenter`, 14 sites in `infantry.yaml`) and so do the ground vehicles. **Aircraft alone name only the two impossible actors** — so the aircraft gap is a one-line omission in a working system, not an absent system.

**A latent path nothing drives.** `ReloadAmmoPool@1/@2` on every airframe is gated `unit.docked && !airborne` (`aircraft-america.yaml:175`, `:205`, and 14 twins). A *captured* LC grants `unit.docked` within 2c0 via `ProximityExternalCondition@UNITDOCKED` (`structures.yaml:400-404`, `ValidRelationships: Ally`), and aircraft declare the receiving `ExternalCondition@UNITDOCKED` (`aircraft.yaml:73-74`). So an aircraft landed beside a captured LC **would** trickle-refill — but nothing, human UI or bot, ever sends one there, and `Rearmable.RearmActors` does not name `logisticscenter`, so the drive-to-host pull cannot select it either.

**The failure mode, stated generally.** `ReturnToBase.ChooseResupplier` filters `ActorsHavingTrait<Reservable>()` by `RearmActors` membership; with an always-empty result `Tick` falls to `QueueChild(new FlyIdle(...)); return true` (**`ReturnToBase.cs:107-108` on `main`**; `:127-128` on this branch). Crucially `Aircraft.ResolveOrder` accepted the order on `RearmActors.Count != 0` alone — a statement about the **rules** standing in for a statement about the **world** — and `QueueActivity(order.Queued: false, ...)` *cancels the current activity*. So a bot `SendDamagedUnitsHome` cancelled a live attack run and replaced it with a hover. That is a second, independent "air units stop being useful" symptom that nobody had attributed to this root cause.

**The dead band is the actual bench.** `AIHelicopterRole.ReEngageHealthPercent` is documented as "HP the helicopter must reach **after repair**" (`AIHelicopterRole.cs:30`) — a recovery bar. With no repair host it can be crossed exactly once, downward, so the interval `[FleeHealthPercent, ReEngageHealthPercent)` is airframes too healthy for any flee path to retire and too damaged for any launch path to pick: **35–75 on every attack heli, 60–90 on both transports** (`aircraft-america.yaml:8-9,112-113,275-276`; `aircraft-russia.yaml:8-9,104-105,276-277`). A 500/800 HP Apache and a 500/600 HP Chinook both sit inside it.

**The fix must not key COMMITMENT off host existence, and this is the part that is easy to get backwards.** Making the bar `hasRepairHost ? recoveryBar : fleeBar` reads naturally and is a step function pointing the wrong way: capturing a logistics center would snap the Apache bar 35 → 75, so **taking ground would make the helicopters more timid**. A host must only ever ADD an option. So the commit floor is the flee bar unconditionally, and the recovery bar governs one thing — whether a damaged airframe is *routed to repair first* (`SendDamagedUnitsHome`). Generalises to any predicate of the form "we have a facility, therefore raise our standards": check the sign before you wire it.

**Separately, `HasRepairHost` cannot flip for an airframe today even in principle.** `Repairable.FindRepairBuilding` filters on `Info.RepairActors`, and aircraft list only `afld`/`hpad` (`aircraft.yaml:80`, `:163`) — `logisticscenter` is absent. So capturing an LC changes nothing for aircraft repair; the path is inert rather than merely untested. Wiring the LC into aircraft `RearmActors`/`RepairActors` is the open decision, and it must be taken knowing it flips both host predicates at once.

**Where the profile-scope claim was wrong — and it was the CODE, not the audit.** `SkipRearmReadyCheck: true` shipped on **both** twins (`ai.yaml:1418`, `:1445`) while its own `[Desc]` (`HelicopterSquadBotModule.cs:186`) and three `ai.yaml` comments all said "experimental only". `06-inherited-misfits.md:266-267` had already read past that and said so — *"routed around by `SkipRearmReadyCheck` on both profiles; and the health gates became unsatisfiable"* — which is exactly right. An earlier revision of this entry blamed the audit for the error; that was itself false and is corrected here. The lesson stands but points elsewhere: **a `[Desc]` claiming a default is not evidence of what shipped — read the YAML.** What actually benched airframes on both profiles was the **health** half, which no flag bypassed anywhere.

**Not every flag near this is a bypass of it.** `UnitBuilderBotModule.SkipRearmBuildingCheck` (`:43`, `HasAdequateAirUnitReloadBuildings` `:1046-1049`) caps aircraft purchases at one per pad. That cap is meaningless under a reinforcement model *regardless* of whether a rearm host exists, so it has an independent reason to exist and is not deletable by fixing the host question. `EvacuateWhenIdle`/`EvacuateIdleTransports` likewise — banking salvage and stopping upkeep is a real doctrine, not a workaround; only their `[Desc]` justifications needed correcting.

**The general tell, sharper than the audit's.** Grepping `~disabled` and then grepping who still names those actors finds this instance. The reusable version is: **any readiness predicate that reads a config list (`RearmActors`, `RepairActors`, `ProductionQueue` names) and concludes something will happen is asserting a world fact from a rules fact.** It degrades silently, because a config list is never empty in a way that looks wrong. Ask the world.

**DEFERRED, deliberately not built on `auto/aircraft-rearm` — the per-unit peel-out is now a complete no-op, and the fix for it is a behavioural change nobody can test today.** `SendDamagedUnitsHome` is the only per-unit health action in the heli FSM, and with no repair host its `ReturnToBase` orders are refused outright (`Aircraft.CanReturnToBase`). So nothing ever pulls an individual airframe out of a fight: only the squad *average* acts, via `CommitHealthThreshold`. Combined with the commit floor now being the flee bar, a squad sitting at ~36% average passes the idle gate and relaunches on the ~75-tick withdraw cycle indefinitely, bounded only by `IsTargetTooHot`.

**The fix that suggests itself, recorded so it is not re-derived from scratch:** drop a unit from `Squad.Units` when it falls below its own `FleeHealthPercent`, rather than ordering it home. Squad membership is nothing but that list (`Squad.cs:23`, `IsValid` is `Units.Count > 0` at `:94`), so a membership change needs no order, no activity and no host — it survives the no-host case that defeats every order-based retreat, and the dropped airframe falls back to the module's idle pool where `IsReadyForMission` will decline to re-recruit it while it stays under the bar.

**Why it is NOT in this branch, which is the part worth keeping.** The risk it addresses was *inferred from reading the code*, not *observed in a match*. The branch already carries one un-run behavioural change (the readiness bars themselves). Adding a second untested behavioural change to fix an unobserved risk is how a clean branch turns into an unattributable regression: when the benchmark moves, there is no way to say which of the two moved it. **Queue it behind a live look at the first change.** The general rule: one un-run behavioural change per branch is a measurement; two is a guess.

**Related, and it lands at the same instant.** Neither host predicate can be true for an airframe today — `Rearmable.RearmActors` and `Repairable.RepairActors` list only `hpad`/`afld`. So `RepairRoutingBar`'s hosted arm and `MemberStillShoots`/`AmmoReadyToLaunch`'s hosted arms are pinned by unit test and by nothing else. Wiring `logisticscenter` into either list flips **both** predicates simultaneously, so all three hosted arms go live together, first-run-in-anger, on the three maps that have an LC. Whoever takes that decision should expect to be the first person ever to execute that code.

## 2026-08-10 — A UNIT ON DEFENSIVE NEVER WALKS TO AN AUTO-TARGET, SO A "SEARCH RADIUS" WIDER THAN THE WEAPON IS NOT A BEHAVIOUR — IT IS A CLAIM ON SOMEONE NOBODY WILL TREAT

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — a unit below `Hunt` never walks to an auto-target (`AutoTarget.cs:635`; `Activities/Attack.cs:280-284`, HoldPosition refuses unconditionally, Defensive only for pure out-of-range — a `tooClose`/`losBlocked` target still gets a `MoveWithinRange`, which the entry omits), plus the `AttackMoveActivity` march-interrupt trap (`:122` scan, unconditional `ChildActivity?.Cancel` at `:176`). `^MEDI` Defensive re-verified at `infantry.yaml:2171`; `HealerAutoTarget` `IsInHealRange` gate at `:127`.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AutoTarget.TickIdle` (`AutoTarget.cs:619`) computes `allowMove = allowMovement && engagementStance >= EngagementStance.Hunt`, and `Attack.TickAttack` (`Attack.cs:258-266`) turns that into a hard refusal: for an auto-targeted attack (`!callerAllowedMove`) on `Defensive`, an out-of-range target returns `UnableToAttack` rather than closing. **Defensive and HoldPosition units engage what is already in range and nothing else.** Only a *direct player order* passes `callerAllowedMove: true`.

The consequence for any "notice things further away" feature: widening a scan radius on a trait that feeds `IOverrideAutoTarget` buys **nothing** on a Defensive unit, because the attack layer is where the walking would have to happen and it declines. Medics default to Defensive (`infantry.yaml`, `^MEDI` `InitialEngagementStance`), so `HealerAutoTarget`'s widened radius had to be paired with an approach on the **idle/follow** path (`AutoFollowAlly`) to mean anything. If a healer trait ever appears to "see" patients it never treats, this gate is the first place to look — not the pathfinder.

**Second-order trap, and this one bites units that are not even the ones you changed.** `AttackMoveActivity.Tick` (`AttackMoveActivity.cs:85-93,144`) re-scans via `autoTarget.ScanForTarget(..., ignoreScanInterval: true)` every 10 ticks *while marching*, and **cancels its move child whenever the scan returns any target** (`ChildActivity?.Cancel(self)`), then queues an attack that a Defensive unit will immediately abandon. So an `IOverrideAutoTarget` that returns targets its owner cannot act on does not merely do nothing — it **interrupts that unit's march every 10 ticks**, indefinitely. `IOverrideAutoTarget` implementations should therefore return only targets that are *actionable right now*, and keep "noticed but not yet reached" state to themselves. `HealerAutoTarget.TryGetAutoTargetOverride` now gates on `IsInHealRange` for exactly this reason.

## 2026-08-10 — THE MEDIC'S "NEVER AUTO-SELECTED" BEHAVIOUR IS AN ACCIDENT OF HAVING NO AMMO, AND GIVING HIM AN AMMO POOL WOULD SILENTLY DELETE IT

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — `SelectionPriorityModifier@OutOfAmmo` (`infantry.yaml:245-248`) permanently demotes any unit with an armament and no `AmmoPool`, because `Armament` grants `weapon-<Name>` (`Armament.cs:260`) and the predicate matches `^AmmoDecoration`'s pip expression (`defaults.yaml:775`). Re-verified no `AmmoPool` anywhere in `^MEDI`'s chain. One phrasing correction banked: `DamagePercent: -5` is on the warhead (`weapons-other.yaml:348`), not on the armament.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`^MEDI` has **no support-unit selection template** — nothing anywhere says "prefer other units over the medic". The behaviour the user relies on (drag-select a squad, the medic is not what gets picked) comes from `^Soldier`'s out-of-ammo selection-priority modifier (`infantry.yaml:245-248`), whose predicate is the `^AmmoDecoration` empty-ammo expression. A medic has **no `AmmoPool` anywhere in its ancestry**, so that predicate is *permanently true* and the medic is *permanently demoted*.

**So the deprioritization is load-bearing on the medic staying ammo-less.** Give `^MEDI` an `AmmoPool` (to meter heals, say), or rename its `primary` armament, and the demotion vanishes without a single line of selection code changing — the medic starts being picked as the representative of every squad selection, and the cause will look nothing like the change that produced it. Heals are unlimited today; if that ever needs to change, the metering must not come from an `AmmoPool`, or the selection template has to be written explicitly first.

Related, from the same pass: **healing is a negative-damage `Armament` on the ordinary attack path** (`^MEDI` `Armament@1`, `Weapon: Heal`, `DamagePercent: -5`), not `RepairsUnits` and not `HealthUnitsAndBuildings`. Its `Heal` target type is granted by `Targetable@Heal`, gated on the `damaged` condition (`infantry.yaml:63-65`, `defaults.yaml:173-175`). That is why clicking an **unhurt** ally produced no order and no cursor at all: `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` returns empty and `AttackBase.AttackOrderTargeter.CanTargetActor` bails before it sets a cursor. Anything that wants to interact with a *healthy* ally has to be a separate order (see `AttendAlly`), because widening the `Heal` target type to undamaged actors would let the heal warhead fire at full-health men.

## 2026-08-10 — A PAUSED ARMAMENT PASSES TARGETING AND THEN DECLINES TO FIRE IN SILENCE, SO "THE ORDER WAS REFUSED" AND "THE ORDER WAS ACCEPTED AND WEDGED" LOOK IDENTICAL ON SCREEN

> **[promoted (mechanism only): → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` filters `IsTraitDisabled` but not `IsTraitPaused` (`AttackBase.cs:448-452`, `// FF TODO Check ammo?` now at `:437`), `CanTargetActor` tolerates pause (`:732`), `Armament.CanFire` declines (`Armament.cs:327`), and `AbandonWhenArmamentsPaused` is the opt-in escape (`AttackBase.cs:72`, default false; consumed `Attack.cs:253`). **ONE CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED:** `^MEDI`'s heal armament carries **no `PauseOnCondition` at all** today — `infantry.yaml:2216-2231` has none, and `:2222` carries a PITFALL forbidding re-adding it. The 2026-08-11 `suppressed >= 10` entry below is the current one; the only surviving gates are `^AT` (`:1702`) and the engineer (`:1915`).]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AttackBase.ChooseArmamentsForTarget` (`AttackBase.cs:429-433`) filters `!a.IsTraitDisabled` and **not** `IsTraitPaused` — there is a `// FF TODO Check ammo?` sitting on the line above, so the omission is known and unresolved. `AttackOrderTargeter.CanTargetActor` then *deliberately* tolerates paused armaments (`AttackBase.cs:703`: `FirstOrDefault(x => !x.IsTraitPaused) ?? armaments.First()`). So a unit whose every armament is paused **accepts the order and shows a cursor**.

What happens next is the trap. `Attack.TickAttack` computes ranges, closes, turns, and reaches `DoAttack`, which calls `Armament.CheckFire` → `CanFire` → `false` on `IsTraitPaused` (`Armament.cs:327`) and returns null. Nothing is fired, nothing is logged, and `TickAttack` still returns `AttackStatus.Attacking`, so `Attack.Tick` returns false. **The activity never completes.** The unit stands aiming at a target it cannot engage for as long as the pause lasts, and because it is never idle, every `INotifyIdle` behaviour it owns — auto-target, auto-follow, auto-rearm — is silenced at the same time.

Measured on the medic (`test-medic-suppressed-gives-up`): `^MEDI`'s heal `Armament@1` carries `PauseOnCondition: suppressed >= 10`, and a wounded man is nearly always a man under fire — so the medic beside him is suppressed too. Right-clicking a *legitimately wounded* soldier therefore produced a medic who walked over, aimed, and healed nobody, indefinitely. **The user reported this as "medics reject heal orders and just stay still", and the order was in fact accepted.** Diagnosing from the report alone sends you to the targeting gate (`Targetable@Heal` needing the `damaged` condition), which is a real refusal path but *not this one* — that path produces no cursor and no order packet at all. **Distinguish the two by whether a cursor appears and whether the unit walks: refusal is silent and stationary from the first frame; the stall walks, arrives, and then does nothing.**

Fix shape used: `AttackBaseInfo.AbandonWhenArmamentsPaused` (default false, so every other unit keeps holding aim through brief pauses), which makes `TickAttack` return `UnableToAttack` when all chosen armaments are paused. Suppression is not brief and a medic's idle behaviour is worth more than his aim, so `^MEDI` opts in. **Anything else with a long-lived `PauseOnCondition` and meaningful idle behaviour is a candidate for the same field** — the failure is invisible in logs and looks like a pathing or order bug.

## 2026-08-10 — THE SILENT-DECLINE WEDGE HAS EXACTLY ONE LIVE ENTRANCE ON A SHORT-RANGE WEAPON, AND THE OBVIOUS GENERALISATION OF THE FIX IS A BUG

> **[promoted (partial): → conventions.md — the `FiringLOS.HasClearLOS` unconditional-true inside two cells (`FiringLOS.cs:77`, so any ≤2-cell weapon is LOS-immune; heal weapon is `1c0`, `weapons-other.yaml:341`) and the do-NOT-widen rationale (`Armament.CanFire` is also false on `IsReloading`/`IsWaitingBurst`/`IsAiming`, so the general form would drop every attack order between shots). **Rejected: narrow** — the `HealerClaimLayer` bidirectional-registry bug is fixed (`HealerClaimLayer.cs:69-71` now checks the forward entry before deleting), so it is an incident report, not reference material.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Follow-up to the paused-armament entry above, from adversarial review of the medic branch. Both facts are worth keeping because each one talks a future reader *out of* a change that looks obviously right.

**The LOS gate cannot produce the wedge at heal range.** `FiringLOS.HasClearLOS` (`FiringLOS.cs:64-77`) returns true unconditionally when the cell-distance² is `< 4` — inside two cells there is no shadow data, so everything is assumed visible. The heal weapon reaches `1c0`, so at every distance a medic could possibly fire, both the per-weapon gate in `Armament.CheckFire` and the unit-level `losBlocked` term in `Attack.TickAttack` are pinned true. **A medic cannot wedge on line of sight**, and the graded-detection system cannot reach him either. Any short-range weapon (≤2 cells) has the same immunity.

**So do NOT widen `AttackBaseInfo.AbandonWhenArmamentsPaused` into "abandon when the unit cannot fire".** `Armament.CanFire` (`Armament.cs:327`) is false on `IsReloading`, `IsWaitingBurst` and `IsAiming` as well as `IsTraitPaused` — the first three are true on ordinary ticks of a perfectly healthy weapon, so the general version would drop every attack order in the game between shots. The field is narrow on purpose: **pause is the only one of those states that can last, and duration is the whole reason the wedge is visible.** The one legitimate widening is the trait-level pause (`attack.IsTraitPaused`), because `Attack.DoAttack` skips every armament wholesale on it; that is now covered.

**Still open, and it is the first place to look if a medic ever wedges again WITHOUT being suppressed.** `Attack.TickAttack:263` sets `needsToMove` from `outOfRange || tooClose || cantInteract || losBlocked`, and `:287` then queues a `MoveWithinRange`. When the mover is *already* inside `maxRange` — i.e. `needsToMove` was set by `cantInteract` (`move is Mobile mobile && !mobile.CanInteractWithGroundLayer(self)`) rather than by distance — that child completes in a single tick having gone nowhere, `TickAttack` re-queues it on the next, and the unit spins non-idle forever. **Same observable symptom as the pause wedge, different cause, and the pause guard does not catch it** (the armaments are live). Not reproduced; recorded because the symptom is indistinguishable by eye and the diagnosis would otherwise start in the wrong place.

**Unrelated invariant, same branch: a two-map claim registry needs its forward entry checked before deletion.** `HealerClaimLayer` keys claims both ways (`claimByHealer`, `claimByPatient`), and a healer's reverse entry outlives his claim — a second healer re-claiming the same patient rewrites `claimByPatient` but not the first healer's `claimByHealer`. So the first healer's later `RemoveClaim` (on death, or on giving up) deleted the *second* healer's live claim, the patient read unclaimed to everyone, and a third healer piled onto the same casualty. Only visible once claims live long enough to overlap, which is what widening the search radius from 1 to 8 cells did. **Any bidirectional registry with the same shape wants `if (forward[b] == a)` before `forward.Remove(b)`.**

## 2026-08-11 — A STALL GUARD WHOSE TRIGGER CONDITION IS ALSO SATISFIED BY SUCCESS, OR: "NOTHING CHANGED" IS NOT "STUCK"

> **[rejected: narrow — the guard bug is fixed; the in-range early-out now precedes `TrackStall` and refreshes its counters (`AutoFollowAlly.cs:118-130`), exactly as the entry prescribes. **The durable half was promoted** → conventions.md: `Mobile.MoveResult` is declared (`Mobile.cs:265`) and read (`MoveAdjacentTo.cs:107`, `MoveCooldownHelper.cs:69,76`) but **never assigned anywhere**, and `InProgress` is enum value 0 — so a move that cannot path never reports failure, and any absence-keyed failure detector must exit on the success states first.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Caught in review of the medic branch, and worth keeping for the shape rather than the instance. `AutoFollowAlly` gained a stall guard because `Mobile.MoveResult` is never assigned and a move that cannot path never reports failure (see the 2026-08-10 entry above) — so the only available evidence of a stall is *the follower has not changed cell for N ticks*. That predicate is true in two completely different situations:

- the follower cannot reach his target — the case the guard is for; and
- the follower has **arrived** and is standing at exactly the distance he was asked to keep.

The guard ran before the in-range early-out, so the second case fell into it. A medic parked correctly beside his squadmate logged four consecutive "no cell change" checks, benched that squadmate for ~100 ticks, and then lagged the squad by up to four seconds — on a repeating cycle. **The branch existed to stop medics being left behind, and it shipped a guard that dropped the escorted man every four seconds precisely because the escort was working.** It passed the branch's own autotest, because that test asserts the patient gets healed and healing happens well inside the first bench cycle.

The general rule: **whenever a failure detector keys on the absence of something (no movement, no ammo gained, no progress, no response), enumerate the success states that also produce that absence and exit on them FIRST.** A detector placed before the success check does not measure failure, it measures stillness — and arrival, completion, and being-already-correct are all still. Mechanically: put the "we're done / we're fine" early-out ahead of the guard, and have that path *refresh* the guard's state rather than merely skipping it, or the counters stay warm and the guard fires the moment anything else briefly stalls.
## 2026-08-10 — `AutoSeekSupplies.ReturnWhenEmpty` DELIBERATELY DECLINES TO INTERRUPT WHEN NO HOST IS IN LEASH, AND THAT DECLINE BRANCH IS WHERE THE STUCK-DRY-UNIT BUG ACTUALLY LIVES

> **[promoted: → economy.md §The vehicle ammo roster — `ReturnWhenEmpty` bounds *what it will interrupt an order for* and is not a guarantee that a dry unit stops attacking. Re-verified: `rearmable == null` early-out (`AutoSeekSupplies.cs:226-227`), the decline branch with its verbatim “an unreachable errand is worse than none” comment (`:281-288`), `ReturnWhenEmptyLeashCells = 30` (`:84`), and the trait's whole footprint — `^Soldier` (`infantry.yaml:228`) and `^E6` (`:1949`), no vehicle anywhere.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Reading `AutoSeekSupplies` (`AutoSeekSupplies.cs:224+`) it is easy to conclude the "dry unit keeps its attack order" complaint is already solved — the trait is an `ITick` that explicitly exists to interrupt a live order on `AmmoPool.AllPoolsEmpty`. It is not solved, and the gap is stated in the trait's own code: when `ChooseResupplier` returns null, the host is out of the world, or it fails `WithinReturnLeash` (`ReturnWhenEmptyLeashCells`, default 30), the trait **flags `NeedsResupply` and leaves the unit's current order alone** — "an unreachable errand is worse than none". That decision is correct on its own terms and should stay.

What it means is that outside the leash the unit keeps an attack order it can never discharge, which is not a neutral state: the attack activities park on it forever (below), so the unit is not merely un-helped, it is **frozen and never idle**, and therefore invisible to every idle-triggered mechanism including `AmmoPool`'s own unleashed dispatch. The trait's gap and the activity's stall compound into a unit deleted from the game in all but name.

- **Two more populations get nothing from the trait at all**: anything without `Rearmable` (the ITick returns immediately on `rearmable == null`) and anything without `AutoSeekSupplies` in its template. **The second of those is every vehicle in the game** — and vehicles are emphatically NOT infinite-ammo, see the file-layout entry below. So for a dry tank there is no seek trait at all, and the guards in the attack activities are the *only* thing that can release it from an order it can never discharge. (An earlier revision of this entry claimed vehicles were infinite-ammo. That was wrong, and the way it was got wrong is itself recorded below.)
- **The reusable rule**: `AutoSeekSupplies.ReturnWhenEmpty` bounds *what it will interrupt an order for*. It is not, and was never claimed to be, a guarantee that a dry unit stops attacking. If you need the latter, it belongs in the attack activities, not in the seek trait.

## 2026-08-10 — THE ATTACK ACTIVITIES NEVER CONSULT AMMO, SO A DRY UNIT HOLDS ITS ATTACK ACTIVITY FOR THE REST OF THE MATCH

> **[promoted (partial): → economy.md — the ammo-blind targeting chain and `AmmoPool.CannotFight` as the correct predicate; the guards are live at `Activities/Attack.cs:117`, `AttackFollow.cs:346`, `AttackMoveActivity.cs:93`. **THE CLOSING PITFALL IS CONTRADICTED:** “`PauseOnCondition` also carries `garrisoned-at-port`, `infantry.yaml:52`” is false — `:52` is **`Mobile`'s** `PauseOnCondition`, the only other use is on `AttackFrontal`, and **no `Armament` in the mod carries `garrisoned-at-port`**, so the stated counterexample does not exist. Two additions banked: `CannotFight` also exempts aircraft (`AmmoPool.cs:216`), and `AttackBase.cs:440-447` now argues the per-armament `!IsTraitPaused` test is the right level for the mixed dry-rifle/loaded-RPG case.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AttackBase.ChooseArmamentsForTarget` (`AttackBase.cs:409-434`) filters on `IsTraitDisabled` only — there is a literal `// FF TODO Check ammo?` at the top of the `Where`. `IsTraitPaused`, which is what `PauseOnCondition: !ammo-primary` actually sets, is never consulted. The consequences run all the way down:

- `AutoTarget.ChooseTarget` uses that same unfiltered call (`AutoTarget.cs:1099`), so **a unit with zero ammo still acquires targets normally.** It is not passively ignored by the targeting layer; it actively signs up for fights.
- `Activities/Attack.cs` `TickAttack` therefore reports `AttackStatus.Attacking`, `DoAttack` calls `CheckFire`, and `Armament.CanFire` silently declines because the armament is ammo-paused. `Tick` returns `false` (`Attack.cs:186-187`) — every tick, forever. The turreted twin is `AttackFollow.cs`'s `AttackActivity.Tick`, which parks on its final `return false`.
- `GetMaximumRangeVersusTarget` (`AttackBase.cs:593-625`) is what makes the stall *stationary* rather than self-correcting: it has an explicit `maxFallback` that returns the paused armament's range "when ALL weapons are out of ammo". So a dry unit computes a perfectly good engagement range, walks to it, and stops. Had it returned `WDist.Zero` the activity would have terminated on its own.
- Because `Actor.IsIdle` is `CurrentActivity == null`, none of this is ever observable to `INotifyBecomingIdle`. **The unit is busy, and what it is busy with is nothing.**

Fixed by testing `AmmoPool.CannotFight` at the top of both attack activities and of `AttackMoveActivity.Tick`. Note the third one is not optional: aborting only the attack children un-sticks the engagement but leaves the attack-move to resume marching, so the unit reaches idle only at the far end of its original order.

**PITFALL for anyone adding a new "can this unit fight" test**: there are four plausible predicates here and three of them are wrong. Not `Rearmable.RearmableAmmoPools` (different question — see the 13-of-14 entry above), not "every armament `IsTraitPaused`" (`PauseOnCondition` also carries `garrisoned-at-port`, `infantry.yaml:52`, so a garrisoned man with a full magazine reads as dry), not the `^AmmoDecoration` red-pip condition (implied by, not equal to). `AmmoPool.CannotFight` / `AllPoolsEmpty` is the one.

## 2026-08-10 — SUPPLY-ROUTE "ATTACK" ORDERS ARE PRESENCE ORDERS, AND A DRY UNIT IS A PERFECTLY GOOD CONTESTER

> **[promoted: → supply-route.md §What an AI should never assume — `AttacksSupplyRoutes` is a **presence** order and the name is the trap. Re-verified: `Activities/AttackSupplyRoute.cs` has zero hits for `Armament`/`CheckFire`/`AttackBase`/`Ammo`; it moves into range (`:84`) and stands (`:100`). `SupplyRouteContestation.RecalculateForces` (`:184-206`, cite exact) scores purely on `Valued.Cost`.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AttacksSupplyRoutes` reads like an attack trait and its order is literally named `AttackSupplyRoute`, so it invites being swept up in any "stop dry units from attacking" change. It must not be. `AttackSupplyRoute` (`Activities/AttackSupplyRoute.cs`) never fires a weapon — it moves into `SupplyRouteContestation.Info.Range` and stands there until the situation resolves — and `SupplyRouteContestation.RecalculateForces` (`SupplyRouteContestation.cs:184-206`) scores the zone purely on `ValuedInfo.Cost` of the actors present, with no reference to ammunition, armaments, or ability to fire.

So an out-of-ammo unit parked on an enemy SR is **doing the whole job the order asked of it**, and the same holds for the allied-SR defensive case. Blocking the order on a dry check would remove one of the few things a dry unit can still usefully do, and it would not even be fixing a stall: the activity has no aim-forever branch, it just stands in the zone contributing value. The name is the trap.

## 2026-08-10 — `vehicles.yaml` CONTAINS ALMOST NO VEHICLES, AND READING IT ALONE TELLS YOU THE OPPOSITE OF THE TRUTH ABOUT VEHICLE AMMUNITION

> **[promoted: → economy.md §The vehicle ammo roster — **all 17 capacity figures re-verified correct**, as are the armed==pooled rule, the pool-less set, the `AttackFrontal`/`AttackTurreted` 2-vs-15 split, the three `Rearmable`-less rocket artillery, and the `vehicles.yaml`-is-not-the-vehicles file-layout trap. **Key-name correction banked, and applied on sight to economy.md, which had it wrong in three places:** the YAML fields are `InitialResupplyBehavior` / `InitialResupplyBehaviorAI` (`AutoTarget.cs:193,196`, chosen at `:473`) — `ResupplyBehavior` is the **enum type** (`:28`), not a settable key. Minor: `iskander`'s `AttackFrontal` is `vehicles-russia.yaml:985`; `TRUK` also overrides to `Evacuate`.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Grepping `mods/ww3mod/rules/ingame/vehicles.yaml` for `AmmoPool` returns one live block (`MNLY`'s 10 mines) and nine commented-out ones, which reads exactly like "vehicles used to have ammo and it was disabled". **That conclusion is false, and I drew it and had to retract it.** Two independent traps stacked:

1. **`vehicles.yaml` holds the shared `^Vehicle` / `^TrackedVehicle` / `^WheeledVehicle` templates plus a handful of unarmed support units** (`MSAR`, `MNLY`, `truk`, `LCCV`). Every actual combat vehicle lives in `vehicles-america.yaml`, `vehicles-russia.yaml` and `vehicles-ukraine.yaml`. The naming invites you to treat one file as the whole subsystem.
2. **The commented-out `AmmoPool` blocks in `vehicles.yaml` are not disabled pools on live units — they are parts of two entirely commented-out ACTORS**, `SandBagLayer` (~`:634`) and `timberwolf` (~`:693`), units that are not in the game at all. Commented out in `296a529c` (2023-06-20, "Commented out some vehicles"). A commented `AmmoPool@1:` line looks identical whether it is a disabled trait or a fragment of a disabled actor.

**The truth: every ARMED vehicle in the game carries a live pool, and the capacities are deliberately small.** Full audit of all four vehicle files, so nobody has to re-derive it:

| file | actor | live pools (capacity) |
|---|---|---|
| `vehicles-america.yaml` | `humvee` | 300 |
| | `m113` | 500 |
| | `bradley` | 900 + 8 |
| | `abrams` | **40** |
| | `m109` | **39** |
| | `m270` | **12** |
| | `strykershorad` | 400 + 8 + 4 |
| | `HIMARS` | **2** |
| `vehicles-russia.yaml` | `btr` | 500 |
| | `bmp2` | 900 + 8 |
| | `t90` | **40** |
| | `giatsint` | **39** |
| | `grad` | 40 |
| | `tos` | **24** |
| | `tunguska` | 180 + 8 |
| | `iskander` | **2** |
| `vehicles-ukraine.yaml` | `t72` | **40** |
| `vehicles.yaml` | `MNLY` | 10 (`mines-ammo`, feeds `Minelayer`, not an armament) |

**The only vehicles with NO pool are the ones with no gun**: `MSAR`, `TRUK`, `LCCV` (unarmed support, all in `vehicles.yaml`), the shared `^Vehicle` / `^WheeledVehicle` / `^TrackedVehicle` / `^Walker` templates, and the two projectile-carrier actors `HIMARSMissile` / `IskanderMissile`. There is no armed vehicle anywhere that shoots without drawing from a pool.

Every armed one carries `PauseOnCondition: !ammo-primary || …` on the armament. At 40 rounds for a main battle tank and 2 for `iskander`/`HIMARS`, a vehicle running dry mid-battle is not an edge case — it is the normal course of a fight.

**Two structural splits inside that roster, both of which I first got wrong by generalising from the tanks:**

- **Attack trait is NOT uniformly `AttackTurreted`.** `giatsint` (`vehicles-russia.yaml:489`) and `iskander` (`:987`) are `AttackFrontal`; the other fifteen are `AttackTurreted`. Since `AttackFrontal.GetAttackActivity` returns `Activities.Attack` and `AttackTurreted` inherits `AttackFollow.AttackActivity`, **the vehicle roster is split across BOTH guarded attack activities.** `Activities/Attack.cs` is therefore not the infantry-only path it looks like — it also carries those two vehicles.
- **Three armed vehicles have no `Rearmable` at all**: `m270`, `grad`, `tos`. Not a filtered pool list — the trait is absent, so `ChooseResupplier` can never find them a host, and the LC push cannot reach them either (it is gated on the recipient declaring `replenish-vehicles`, which only `himars` and `iskander` do). **Once spent they can never rearm by any mechanism in the game.** That is deliberate: they are exactly the rocket artillery that overrides `ResupplyBehavior: Evacuate`, so the design answer for a spent Grad is "drive off the map for a refund", not "go and reload". Do not read "vehicles rearm at the Logistics Centre" as covering all of them.

Two consequences that matter more than the file layout:

- **No vehicle has `AutoSeekSupplies`.** None of that trait's machinery — neither the idle seek nor `ReturnWhenEmpty` — applies to a single one of them, whatever their `Rearmable` status. So whatever releases a dry tank from an attack order has to live in the attack activities; there is no seek trait to fall back on.
- **`AttackTurreted` derives from `AttackFollow` and does not override `GetAttackActivity`, so the fifteen turreted vehicles run `AttackFollow.AttackActivity`** — the busiest attack path in the mod by unit count, not a rare one. The remaining two (`giatsint`, `iskander`) run `Activities.Attack` alongside the infantry, per the split above.

**MNLY is the one actor whose live pool is invisible to all of this**, and it is worth knowing why: it has no `Armament` and does not inherit `^AutoTarget`, so it has no `AttackBase`, no `AttackMove` and no `AttacksSupplyRoutes`. A minelayer that has laid all ten mines reads as `AllPoolsEmpty` — but it can never hold an attack order in the first place, so nothing that gates on emptiness can reach it. Check that before assuming a dry-unit rule "also affects the minelayer".

**Reusable rule: before concluding anything about "all vehicles", run `for f in $(grep -rl X mods/ww3mod/rules/); do …` rather than grepping the file whose name matches the concept.** The per-faction split means the file named after a category is frequently the least representative member of it.

## 2026-08-10 — ENDING A DRY UNIT'S ATTACK ACTIVITY HANDS IT STRAIGHT BACK TO `AutoTarget.TickIdle`, WHICH RE-ISSUES THE SAME ATTACK — the guard needs the unit to come to rest OUT of weapon range to settle

> **[promoted (partial): → conventions.md — the re-acquisition mechanism (`ScanOnIdle` true `AutoTarget.cs:65`; `ChooseTarget` calls the ammo-blind `ChooseArmamentsForTarget` at `:1336`/`:1530` so a dry unit re-acquires; the in-range armament filter below `Hunt` is what actually settles it; throttled to the 16–32-tick scan interval, `infantry.yaml:289-290`; `Actor.cs:287-302`'s mutually-exclusive arms mean a re-issued attack cannot stomp a queued errand). **Rejected: narrow** — the measured 246/250 idle and ~62-tick cadence are properties of one scenario, as the entry itself says.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AutoTarget` is `INotifyIdle` with `ScanOnIdle` defaulting to true (`AutoTarget.cs:64`, `:606-622`), so the tick after an attack activity ends, an idle unit rescans and `ScanAndAttack` queues a fresh attack via `AttackTarget`. `ChooseTarget` still does not consult ammo (it calls the same unfiltered `ChooseArmamentsForTarget`), so a dry unit re-acquires perfectly well. **Ending the activity does not, on its own, mean the unit stays idle.**

What actually stops the loop is a range coincidence: `ChooseTarget` filters armaments to those already in range whenever `allowMove` is false, and `allowMove` is false for every engagement stance below Hunt. A unit that halts *outside* its own weapon range therefore finds no candidate and rests. A dry unit sitting *inside* weapon range of a visible enemy will instead cycle — queue attack, guard ends it, go idle, re-queue.

**Two bounds on that cycle, both of which I originally got wrong by describing it as per-tick:**

- **It is throttled to one pass per scan interval, not one per tick.** `ScanForTarget` returns immediately unless `nextScanTime <= 0`, and re-arms it to `SharedRandom.Next(MinimumScanTimeInterval, MaximumScanTimeInterval)` on every scan (`AutoTarget.cs:934-937`) — 16–32 ticks for WW3MOD infantry. So the unit is idle for the whole interval and non-idle for roughly the single tick the re-issued attack survives, not flickering at tick resolution.
- **It cannot happen to a vehicle at all**, for a reason that is a defect in its own right (see the scan-radius entry below): no vehicle pins `AutoTarget.ScanRadius`, so a dry one's scan range collapses to zero and it acquires nothing to re-attack. Only infantry — which pin `ScanRadius: 25` at `infantry.yaml:288` — can enter this cycle.

That cycle is not inert, and mostly in a good way: each pass through idle fires `AmmoPool.INotifyBecomingIdle` → `AutoRearmIfAllEmpty`, so the moment any resupplier is reachable the unit is dispatched and the loop terminates on its own. It is a bounded retry, and strictly better than the permanent freeze it replaces — which asked for resupply exactly once and then never again. With no resupplier anywhere the unit is stationary and harmless, but `IsIdle` alternates rather than latching, which matters to anything gating on it (bot modules, `StarvingRecruitGate`, selection filters).

**It cannot race the resupply it dispatches.** `Actor.Tick` (`:286-301`) is `if (!wasIdle && IsIdle) { OnBecomingIdle…; RunActivity again } else if (wasIdle) { TickIdle… }` — the two arms are mutually exclusive, so the tick that dispatches a resupply is never the tick that re-issues an attack, and a re-acquired attack cannot stomp a queued errand.

**MEASURED, not predicted** (`test-dry-inrange-idle-oscillation`: a dry rifleman 8 cells from a live target, no resupplier anywhere, sampling `IsIdle` every tick for 250 ticks): **idle 246/250 ticks (98%), busy 4, 8 transitions.** The cycle is real — 4 complete idle→busy→idle rounds in 10 s — and it is cheap: one busy tick per round, idle 98% of the time. Nothing pathological, nothing resembling per-tick churn.

The cadence came out **slower than the scan interval alone predicts**: ~62 ticks per round against `nextScanTime`'s 16–32. I did not instrument why (a scan that finds no candidate still re-arms the timer, so not every scan yields a re-issue), so treat 62 as "this setup", not as a constant.

**What it DOES cost is shared-RNG stream position** — see the `SharedRandom` entry below. At 4 rounds per 10 s, one dry in-range soldier consumes on the order of a dozen extra synced draws per 10 s that the pre-fix frozen unit consumed none of. That is the part worth disclosing on a benchmark branch, not the CPU.

**If this needs closing, the place is `AutoTarget` — teaching the scan itself not to acquire for a unit that cannot fire — not another guard in the activities.** That is the same `// FF TODO Check ammo?` at `AttackBase.cs:428` seen from the other end, and it would be a behavioural change to opportunity fire, so it wants its own branch and its own measurement rather than being smuggled in alongside the activity guards.

## 2026-08-11 — A PAUSED ARMAMENT SHRINKS THE UNIT'S AUTOTARGET SCAN RADIUS TO ZERO, so an EMP'd / suppressed / badly damaged / dry vehicle stops SEEING as well as stops shooting

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — a paused armament collapses the autotarget scan radius to zero. Re-verified: the range pick is `Info.ScanRadius > 0 ? ... : ab.GetMaximumRange()` at `AutoTarget.cs:1040` and `:1095` (entry cited `:945`), `ScanRadius` defaults `-1` (`:68`), and `GetMaximumRange()` skips `IsTraitDisabled` **or `IsTraitPaused`**, returning `WDist.Zero` when all are paused. `ScanRadius: 25` on exactly two infantry lines (`infantry.yaml:288`, `:2317` — entry said `:2280`), no vehicle, three maps pin 40. The shipped pause set was re-derived by owning trait rather than by raw grep: `garrisoned-at-port` and `build-incomplete` are **not** armament-level and were dropped from the promoted list.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

`AutoTarget.ScanForTarget` picks its scan range as `Info.ScanRadius > 0 ? WDist.FromCells(Info.ScanRadius) : ab.GetMaximumRange()` (`AutoTarget.cs:945`). The fallback is the trap: `AttackBase.GetMaximumRange` (`:545-566`) skips every armament that is `IsTraitDisabled` **or `IsTraitPaused`**. So when all armaments are paused it returns `WDist.Zero`, the scan circle is a point, and the unit auto-acquires nothing at all.

**`ScanRadius` is pinned on exactly two lines of shipped unit rules, both infantry** (`infantry.yaml:288` and `:2280`, `ScanRadius: 25`). **No vehicle pins it**, so every vehicle in the game runs the engine default `-1` and takes the fallback. Three shipped maps pin it map-locally (`arena-tank-duel`, `river-zeta-ww3/scenarios.yaml`, `shellmap-open-field`), which is also why a bug here can hide in exactly the scenarios people test with.

**This is not an ammo story — ammo is just the case I arrived through.** Any `PauseOnCondition` on the armament does it, and the shipped set is broad: `empdisable` (46 uses), `unit.docked` (14+), `disabled` (13), `heavy-damage-attained`, `garrisoned-at-port`, `suppressed >= 10`, `inwater`, `firing`, `build-incomplete`. Concretely, on current rules:

- An **EMP'd** vehicle does not merely hold fire, it goes blind and forgets to look.
- A vehicle below 50% HP has `heavy-damage-attained` on its armament (15 vehicles), so a damaged tank's autotarget radius collapses at the same instant its gun locks.
- A **suppressed** unit (`suppressed >= 10`) stops scanning — directly relevant to the suppression work, since "suppressed units don't return fire" and "suppressed units cannot see targets to return fire at" are different mechanisms with different recovery behaviour.
- A unit **`inwater`** or garrisoned likewise.

**Consequence for anyone reasoning about, or testing, autotarget behaviour under a pause condition: the unit is not just weapons-tight, it is sensor-dead, and it will not re-acquire the instant the condition lifts either** — it re-acquires on its next scan tick. Pre-existing, not introduced by the ammo-guard branch and deliberately not fixed there; the branch only made it *visible*, because a dry vehicle is the first case where somebody asked "why didn't it re-acquire?". If it is ever fixed, the honest fix is for the fallback to use unpaused-if-any-else-all range (the same `maxFallback` shape `GetMaximumRangeVersusTarget` already uses at `AttackBase.cs:593-625`), not to sprinkle `ScanRadius` onto every vehicle.

## 2026-08-11 — A UNIT THAT BECOMES IDLE CONSUMES `SharedRandom`, so "it now goes idle instead of freezing" is a DETERMINISM change, not only a behaviour change

> **[promoted: → conventions.md §Engine behaviors that surprise — becoming idle consumes `SharedRandom`, so a change to whether a unit idles is a determinism change. Re-verified: `WithInfantryBody` draws twice at `:206-207`, the state re-arms via `PlayStandAnimation` (`:128`, called from `:192`), 12 soldier classes declare `IdleSequences`, `AutoTarget` draws once per scan at `:1087`, and `TurnOnIdle` is used by no ww3mod rule. Banked with the operational consequence: re-take the `@stable` baseline, do not diff replays across it.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Idle is not a quiet state in this engine. Three shipped consumers draw from the synced RNG on the idle path:

- **`WithInfantryBody.TickIdle` draws TWICE** per `Waiting → Idle` transition — `IdleSequences.Random(self.World.SharedRandom)` and `SharedRandom.Next(MinIdleDelay, MaxIdleDelay)` (`:206-207`, delays 30–110). Gated on `IdleSequences.Length > 0`, which 12 soldier classes in `infantry.yaml` declare.
- **That state re-arms itself.** `WithInfantryBody.Tick` (`:190-192`) calls `PlayStandAnimation` — which sets `state = Waiting` (`:128`) — whenever a unit in `Idle`/`IdleAnimating` becomes non-idle. So every idle→busy→idle cycle buys a fresh pair of draws, and a permanently idle soldier also keeps drawing forever via the `Idle → IdleAnimating → PlayStandAnimation → Waiting` animation loop.
- **`AutoTarget.ScanForTarget` draws once per scan** to re-arm `nextScanTime` (`:937`).
- `TurnOnIdle` draws too (`:55-56`) but **is not used anywhere in WW3MOD rules** — noted so nobody re-checks it.

**Why this matters more than it looks.** Before the ammo guard, a dry unit under orders was never idle, so it consumed none of these draws for the rest of the match. Now it goes idle and starts consuming them — and `SharedRandom` is a single synced stream, so every draw shifts stream position for **every** later consumer in the match, not just for that unit. The behavioural change is local; the RNG consequence is global.

**So the benchmark-relevant statement is not "bots issue the same orders and therefore see the guard".** It is: *dry units now become idle, which feeds every idle-triggered trait and every `IsIdle`-gated bot census that previously never saw them, and moves the shared RNG stream.* Any @stable baseline taken before this cannot be compared tick-for-tick with one taken after, even where the tactical outcome is identical. Re-take the baseline; do not diff replays across it.

This is a property of the engine's idle path, not of the guard — but the guard is what makes units reach it, so it is the guard's disclosure to carry.

## 2026-08-11 — RELEASE BRANDING RECON: the load screen has no logo slot filled, the main menu has no background image *by design*, and every installer icon is still the OpenRA SDK "Ex" placeholder

> **[promoted (partial): → architecture.md §Asset pipeline — only the **mechanism** half: the load screen is a compositor with no full-screen background path (`LogoStripeLoadScreen.cs:51-52`, `CustomBar` bar at `:62-79`), the 2x/3x files buy sharpness not size (`SheetLoadScreen.cs:47-89`, rect × density then sprite × 1/density), and the two dead icon paths (`LauncherIcon` defined nowhere; no `SDL_SetWindowIcon` in `engine/`). The empty 256×256 logo rect was re-confirmed by decode (65 536 px, 0 with non-zero alpha). **Rejected: the status half is tracker material — and FOUR CLAIMS ARE NOW CONTRADICTED:** `label-openra` **is** overridden (`mods/ww3mod/languages/en.ftl:28` = “WW3MOD”, landed `12db45a8`); `ModContent.InstallPromptMessage` was rewritten to WW3MOD prose (`mod.yaml:398`); `ModCredits` is live with `credits.txt` present (`mod.yaml:449-451`); and the `logos` collection is **no longer consumed** — `chrome/gamesave-loading.yaml` was rewritten to `ColorBlock`s and references it nowhere. The entry's closing cross-checkable claim is therefore half-dead.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Read-only audit of every surface that makes the build look finished vs. mod-in-progress, done against `main @ bd7b6bb2`. The durable part is the **mechanism** of each surface — several are not "swap a PNG", and guessing wrong wastes an art pass.

**1. The load screen is a compositor, not a full-screen image.** `LoadScreen: LogoStripeLoadScreen` (`mod.yaml:258-263`) → `engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/LoadScreens/LogoStripeLoadScreen.cs:21`. It draws exactly three things: a **logo sprite cut from rect `(0,0,256,256)`** of the sheet (`:51`), a stripe cut from `(258,0,253,256)` (`:52`), and text. There is **no code path in this class that renders a full-screen background** — the screen is otherwise black. Handing it a 1920×1080 painting cannot work without a new `SheetLoadScreen` subclass.
- **`CustomBar: true` (`mod.yaml:263`) makes the stripe half of the PNG dead.** `:62-79` replaces it with a solid `RGB(35,35,35)` bar 160 px tall, full width, with 1 px `RGB(60,60,60)` edges, then draws "WW3MOD" in the `TitleLarge` font (`:98-108`). The `stripe` sprite is only used in the `else` at `:80-81`. So `loadscreen.png`'s right-hand 253×256 region is currently loaded and never drawn.
- **The logo region is 100 % transparent.** Decoded the PNG: rect `(0,0,256,256)` = 65 536 px, **0 with non-zero alpha**. The stripe region is 50 % opaque (the blue/red split). Compare `engine/mods/ra/uibits/loadscreen.png`, which has the Soviet star in that rect — WW3MOD's copy is a *deliberate erase* (no md5 matches RA for any `uibits/*.png`). **So the load screen today renders a gray bar and text with an empty 256×256 hole in the middle**, which is the single most "unfinished" frame a new player sees.
- **Resolution independence: the extra pixels buy sharpness only, never size.** `SheetLoadScreen.cs:59-77` picks `Image`/`Image2x`/`Image3x` purely from `Game.Renderer.WindowScale` (>1 → 2x, >2 → 3x), and `CreateSprite` (`:87-90`) multiplies the rect by `density` **and** scales the sprite by `1f/density`. The logo is therefore always 256×256 *logical* px, centred, at every window size — it never stretches, crops, or scales with the window. The 2x/3x files must place their regions at `density × rect`, i.e. the stripe starts at x=516 (2x) / x=774 (3x), not at 2×256.

**2. The main menu has no background asset — it renders a live game.** `mod.yaml:181` uses stock `common|chrome/mainmenu.yaml`; there is **no `mods/ww3mod/chrome/mainmenu.yaml`** (grep for `MAINMENU` under `mods/ww3mod/` returns nothing). In that file the `Background@BORDER` and `Image@LOGO` widgets are **commented out** (`engine/mods/common/chrome/mainmenu.yaml:20-28`); what fills the screen is `WorldInteractionController` + `ShellmapViewportController` at `WINDOW_WIDTH/HEIGHT` (`:4-9`) playing `FirstTimeShellmap: River Zeta WW3` (`mod.yaml:7`). Adding a static splash is a **chrome + ChromeProvider-collection change**, not a file drop, and it means giving up the live-map background.
- The `logos` collection *does* exist (`mods/ww3mod/chrome.yaml:732-735`, region `logo: 0,0,256,256` inheriting `^LoadScreen`) and **is** consumed — by `mods/ww3mod/chrome/gamesave-loading.yaml:15-16`. So the empty logo rect blanks the save-load screen too, not just the load screen.

**3. Installer/exe icons are the OpenRA mod-SDK placeholder, and the mod-chooser icon is byte-identical stock RA.**
- `mods/ww3mod/icon.png` / `-2x` / `-3x` (32/64/96 px) are **md5-identical to `engine/mods/ra/icon*.png`** — the Soviet star. Read by literal filename at `engine/OpenRA.Game/ExternalMods.cs:135-143`, base64'd into the launcher registration; missing files are silently skipped, so there is no error to notice.
- `packaging/artwork/icon_*.png` (9 sizes, 16→1024) are the black **"Ex" (Example mod) glyph**. Every platform installer derives from them: Windows `.ico` from **16, 24, 32, 48, 256 only** (`packaging/windows/buildpackage.sh:112`, applied via rcedit `:117`); macOS `.icns` from **16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512** (`packaging/macos/buildpackage.sh:166-173`, also reused as the DMG volume icon `:191`); Linux hicolor from **16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024** (`packaging/linux/buildpackage.sh:126-130` — note **24×24 is unused on Linux**, and 1024 is unused on Windows *and* macOS).
- **`icon_scalable.svg` does not exist**; `packaging/linux/buildpackage.sh:122-123` installs it if present (stock ships one).
- **Two icon paths that look real and are not:** (a) `<ApplicationIcon>$(LauncherIcon)</ApplicationIcon>` (`engine/OpenRA.WindowsLauncher/OpenRA.WindowsLauncher.csproj:4`) — **`LauncherIcon` is defined nowhere in the repo**, so it resolves empty and the exe icon comes solely from rcedit. (b) There is **no `SDL_SetWindowIcon` call anywhere in `engine/`** — the window is created bare at `Sdl2PlatformWindow.cs:248`. A runtime `icon.png` for the window is simply not wired up, so there is no such asset to author.

**4. Text branding that ships stock.** The main-menu panel header is `Text: label-openra` → **"OpenRA"** (`engine/mods/common/fluent/chrome.ftl:36`), and `mods/ww3mod/languages/en.ftl` does **not** override it. `mod.yaml:3-5` still carries `Version: release-20230225` (the *engine* version reused as the mod version, and it is what `ExternalMods.Register` writes as the mod's version, `ExternalMods.cs:126`), `Website: https://www.openra.net`, and `WebIcon32:` pointing at openra.net's `ra_32x32.png`. `MainMenuLogic.cs:277` hardcodes `"WW3MOD — Pre-Alpha"`. `ModContent.InstallPromptMessage` (`mod.yaml:396-398`) still reads "Red Alert requires artwork…". `mod.config:47,50` point at openra.net. `ModCredits` is commented out (`mod.yaml:447-449`) and no `credits.txt` exists, so the Credits tab shows engine credits only.

**5. What is already done and should NOT be re-made.** `uibits/flags.png` (+2x/3x) is fully WW3-specific — US, Russia, EU, China, Ukraine, NATO, a BRICS composite, Arabian/Iraq/Syria/Jordan — and the `?` tiles at `chrome.yaml:481-486` are the **standard OpenRA random-faction convention**, not placeholders. No `uibits/*.png` md5-matches its RA counterpart, so sidebar/dialog/glyphs are all mod work. Map `map.png` previews are **engine-generated one-px-per-cell thumbnails** (66×34 … 128×128), not authored art. Map `Author:` fields preserve the original OpenRA map authors (Medium Tank, ZxGanon, Azmac, …) — correct attribution for ported maps; leave them.

**Cross-checkable claim for whoever acts on this:** if you replace only `packaging/artwork/*` and `mods/ww3mod/icon*.png`, the game still boots to an empty 256×256 hole on the load screen and a panel headed "OpenRA". Those two are `uibits/loadscreen*.png` and a `label-openra` override, and neither is an icon.

## 2026-08-11 — CAMEOS CAN SKIP SHP AND THE PALETTE ENTIRELY: an RGBA PNG is a fully correct cameo, because the one caveat that blocks loose PNGs for units (no player-colour remap) is exactly the property a cameo never uses

> **[promoted: → architecture.md §Asset pipeline — cameos are the third case the 2026-07-28 PngSheet entry does not name, and the remap caveat is void for them: `IconPalette` defaults to `chrome` with `IconPaletteIsPlayerPalette = false` (`Buildable.cs:42-47`, owner appended only when set, `ProductionPaletteWidget.cs:614`), that flag appears nowhere in `mods/ww3mod/`, and `chrome` IS `temperat.pal` (`palettes.yaml:58-62`). All 15 `*russiaicon.shp` re-confirmed md5-identical to their america twins with sequences already pointed, `dr.russia` the exception. **One narrowing banked:** `ResolveTextureIndex` returns 0 for RGBA only when the palette has **no colour shift** (`SpriteRenderer.cs:118-129`), not “regardless of what the caller passed” — the conclusion holds for cameos because `chrome` has no shift. Canvas-size claim re-measured: 176 cameos at 64×48, 40 at 60×48.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Read-only recon against `main` @ `bd7b6bb2`, for the "give Russian infantry their own cameos" art task. This **narrows** the 2026-07-28 PngSheet entry (~:1195, promoted to `architecture.md` §Asset pipeline), which correctly warns that loose PNGs lose team-colour remap and are therefore "wrong for team-coloured units, good for decoration art". Cameos are a third case that entry does not name, and for them the warning is void.

- **A cameo is never drawn through a player palette, so the remap caveat cannot bite.** `BuildableInfo.IconPalette` defaults to `"chrome"` with `IconPaletteIsPlayerPalette = false` (`engine/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildable.cs:40-47`); `ProductionPaletteWidget` only appends the owner name when that bool is set (`ProductionPaletteWidget.cs:537`). `IconPaletteIsPlayerPalette` appears **nowhere** in `mods/ww3mod/`, and the mod's `chrome` palette is a plain `PaletteFromFile` with `AllowModifiers: false` (`rules/palettes.yaml:58-62`) — not a `PlayerColorPalette`. So indices 80–95 in a cameo render as their fixed `temperat.pal` colours for every player.
- **And RGBA sprites discard the palette reference outright.** `ResolveTextureIndex` returns 0 — i.e. no palette — for any sprite whose channel is RGBA, regardless of what the caller passed (`engine/OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteRenderer.cs:126-129`, comment: *"PERF: Remove useless palette assignments for RGBA sprites"*). `SheetBuilder.FrameTypeToSheetType` maps `Rgba32`/`Bgra32` to the RGBA sheet (`SheetBuilder.cs:52-64`). A 32-bit PNG cameo is therefore pure truecolour and **needs no indexing, no `temperat.pal` conformance, and no `tools/sprite` round-trip**. *Detector for the general shape: before inheriting a caveat, check whether the consumer actually exercises the mechanism the caveat is about — "PNG loses remap" is only a cost where remap is used.*
- **ww3mod's `chrome` palette IS `temperat.pal`** (`palettes.yaml:58-62`) — the same file as the base actor palette (`:50`). Non-obvious, and it means `tools/sprite/validate.py`'s temperat.pal drift check is already the right check for cameos too if the SHP path is taken; there is no separate cameo palette to hunt for. (`chrometd` = `temperattd.pal`, `:25-28`, used by two vehicle/defense entries only.)
- **Cameo canvas size is not a constraint the widget enforces.** `IconSize: 62, 46` (`chrome/ingame-player.yaml:1295`) sizes the *slot*; the sprite is drawn by `WidgetUtils.DrawSpriteCentered` (`WidgetUtils.cs:86-89`) at `pos - 0.5 * s.Size`, with the sprite's own `Offset` added downstream (`SpriteRenderer.cs:135`) — **never scaled and never clipped**. Existing cameos are accordingly a mix of 60×48 and 64×48 and both overhang the 46px slot by a row. So "match the target size exactly" is a consistency convention, not an engine requirement.
- **`--png` reconstructs the full canvas, so the "auto-sliced PNG loses the anchor" trap does not apply to a single-frame cameo.** By default (no `--nopadding`) `ConvertSpriteToPngCommand` exports at `frame.FrameSize` and re-applies `frame.Offset` into the padded image (`ConvertSpriteToPngCommand.cs:60-61`). A SHP cameo's trimmed frame + offset (`ShpTDLoader.cs:145-153`) therefore round-trips to a full-canvas PNG whose art sits where it sat; loaded back as a PngSheet the whole image is one frame at `Offset = 0`, centred — which is the same place. Geometry survives SHP→PNG→PngSheet **for this shape of asset** specifically because it is one full-canvas frame.
- **The Russian infantry cameos are already wired and are byte-identical duplicates of the US art** (as of `bd7b6bb2`). All 15 of `{e1,e2,e3,e4,e6,medi,sn,ar,mt,at,aa,sf,tl,spy,tecn}russiaicon.shp` md5-match their `…americaicon.shp` twin, and `sequences-infantry.yaml` already points `<unit>.russia` at the russia-named file. So new Russian cameo art is a **file-content swap with zero YAML edits** — the common assumption that new cameos need sequence work is wrong here. The one real exception is `dr.russia`, which shares `dricon` with `dr.america` (`sequences-infantry.yaml`, `dr.russia:` block) and would need a new sequence line plus a new file.

**Cross-checkable claim for whoever acts on this:** drop a 32-bit RGBA `e1russiaicon.png` into `mods/ww3mod/bits/misc/icons/` renamed to `e1russiaicon.shp` (no YAML edit — `PngSheetLoader` sniffs magic bytes, not extension, `PngSheetLoader.cs:49`) and the Conscript cameo changes with full truecolour and correct placement. If it renders as a palette-mangled mess, the RGBA branch at `SpriteRenderer.cs:126` is not being taken and this entry is wrong.

**Not verified:** no screenshot was taken of a PNG in an actual cameo slot — the 2026-07-28 PngSheet validation covered world actors, not `ProductionPaletteWidget`. The chain above is read from code only.

## 2026-08-11 — AUDIO RECON: the mod ships ONE playable music track, `Length:` is not a YAML field at all, and Ogg support is a one-word change that is currently switched off

> **[promoted: → architecture.md §Audio pipeline — and **already acted on**: `aee3a02e` (“Enable Ogg Vorbis, drop the unreachable arabs/ voice set, document the music recipe”) landed the `SoundFormats` change, the `MusicInfo`-four-keys / no-`Length:` fact, the silent-drop-on-missing-file trap and the loose-file-over-`scores.mix` rule. **The heading is therefore STALE:** `mod.yaml:327` now reads `SoundFormats: Aud, Wav, Ogg`, and `mods/ww3mod/bits/sounds/arabs/` has been deleted (238 audio files remain, not 270). Everything else re-verified intact (88 declared tracks vs one shipped file; music content package still has no `Download:`; victory/defeat stings still resolve into the undownloadable `scores.mix`; the `Mp3Loader` 0xfbff sniffer). The licensing-exposure survey is tracker material and was not banked.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

Read-only survey of the audio stack ahead of sourcing replacement music for release. Verified against `main` @ `bd7b6bb2`. Six findings, in rough order of how much they change what you'd do.

**1. `SoundFormats` is the gate, and it is set narrower than the engine can do.** `mods/ww3mod/mod.yaml:325` reads `SoundFormats: Aud, Wav`. That string is turned into loader instances by name: `ModData.cs:80` calls `ObjectCreator.GetLoaders<ISoundLoader>`, which resolves each entry as `FindType(format + "Loader")` (`ObjectCreator.cs:169`). So the list is literally class-name prefixes. `OggLoader` and `Mp3Loader` both exist in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/AudioLoaders/`, that assembly is already loaded (`mod.yaml:159`), and the decoders are already NuGet dependencies — `NVorbis 0.10.5` and `MP3Sharp 1.0.5` at `OpenRA.Mods.Common.csproj:10-11`. **Adding `Ogg` to that one line enables Vorbis with no code change and no new dependency.** No upstream mod does this (`ra`, `cnc`, `d2k`, `ts` all ship `Aud, Wav`), so there is no precedent to copy, but nothing is missing either.

**2. There is no `Length:` field in music YAML — it is decoded at load time, and it is cosmetic.** `MusicInfo`'s MiniYaml constructor (`MusicInfo.cs:26-39`) reads exactly four keys: `Hidden`, `VolumeModifier`, `Extension`, `Filename`. Nothing else. `Length` is `{ get; private set; }` (`:23`) and is only ever assigned in `Load()` (`:41-63`) by handing the stream to each registered sound loader and taking `soundFormat.LengthInSeconds`. It is consumed solely for display — the `M:SS` label and the track list (`MusicPlayerLogic.cs:98-99, 148, 165-167`). **Playlist advance never reads it**: `MusicPlaylist.Play()` calls `Game.Sound.PlayMusicThen(currentSong, PlayNextSong)` (`MusicPlaylist.cs:165`) and the next track is triggered by the audio backend's completion callback (`Sound.cs:230-245`). A wrong length cannot desync or stall a playlist. Anyone porting a "get the Length right" habit from another engine is solving a non-problem here.

**3. A registered track that cannot be opened is silently dropped, not an error.** `MusicInfo.Load` sets `Exists` only if `fileSystem.TryOpen` succeeds (`:43-48`), and `Ruleset.InstalledMusic` is `Music.Where(m => m.Value.Exists)` (`Ruleset.cs:95`). `MusicPlaylist` builds its playlist from `InstalledMusic` (`MusicPlaylist.cs:70-77`). **So `music.yaml` is a superset declaration, not a manifest of what ships** — it currently declares 88 tracks and, on a stock install, resolves exactly one. Default extension when `Extension:` is omitted is `aud` (`MusicInfo.cs:37`), which is why every unqualified entry in `music.yaml` is looking for a `.aud`.

**4. The default install has no music, because the music content package is the only one with no download.** `mod.yaml:415-417` declares `music: Base Game Music` with `TestFiles: .../scores.mix` and `Sources:`, but — unlike `base`, `aftermathbase` and `cncdesert` — **no `Download:` key**, and `installer/downloads.yaml` has no music entry. Quick Install therefore cannot fetch it (`mod.yaml:396` says so in the prompt text: *"without music or videos"*). The only music file in the repo is `mods/ww3mod/bits/sounds/music/journey.aud`, registered at `rules/sound/music.yaml:81`. **A player who does Quick Install hears "Journey" (Red Alert: Retaliation) on loop and nothing else** — `GetSong` wraps a one-entry playlist back onto itself (`MusicPlaylist.cs:215-231`).

**5. Victory and defeat stings are wired but no-op on that same default install.** `rules/world.yaml:9-11` sets `VictoryMusic: score` / `DefeatMusic: map` on `^BaseWorld`. Both are `Hidden: true` entries (`music.yaml:20-22, 33-35`) that live in `scores.mix` — i.e. in the package that cannot be downloaded. `IGameOver.GameOver` guards on `SongExists`, which requires `.Exists` (`MusicPlaylist.cs:115-120, 142-156`), so with no music installed the game simply does not change track at game end. **There is no `StartingMusic` and no `BackgroundMusic` anywhere in the mod** — grep returns only those two lines — so there is no dedicated menu theme or briefing track either; the shell map just starts a random playlist entry (`MusicPlaylist.cs:91`).

**6. Mount order decides overrides, and loose folders beat `.mix` archives here.** `FileSystem.TryOpen` / `TryGetPackageContaining` both resolve with `LastOrDefault` over the mounted packages (`FileSystem.cs:216, 244`), so **later mounts win**. `~scores.mix` is mounted at `mod.yaml:33`; `ww3mod|bits/sounds/music` at `mod.yaml:83`. A loose file dropped in that folder therefore shadows a same-named track inside `scores.mix`. Also worth knowing: the `~` prefix means *optional* (`FileSystem.cs:86-112`) — a missing `.mix` is not a startup failure, which is exactly why the music gap is invisible rather than loud.

**Loader constraints worth knowing before exporting anything.** Both `OggFormat` and `Mp3Format` hard-code `SampleBits => 16` (`OggLoader.cs:40`, `Mp3Loader.cs:66`) and pass channels/rate straight through to OpenAL, which only distinguishes mono/stereo × 8/16-bit (`OpenAlSoundEngine.cs:109-114`) — so ≥3 channels is silently mis-sent and must be avoided; sample rate is unconstrained. `WavReader` accepts PCM, MS-ADPCM and IMA-ADPCM only, and throws `NotSupportedException` on anything else (`WavReader.cs:21, 61-62`); its `lengthInSeconds` divides the **whole stream length** including headers (`:69`), so WAV durations read slightly long. `Mp3Loader`'s sniffer is narrow: it accepts an `ID3` tag or a frame sync of exactly `0xfbff` (`Mp3Loader.cs:29-40`), so an MP3 with no ID3 tag that starts `FF F3`/`FF FA` will be rejected as "not an MP3" — another reason to prefer Ogg.

**Licensing exposure (the reason this survey exists).** Two distinct problems, and the second is the worse one. *(a) Inherited at runtime:* ~69% of referenced audio has no file in the repo and resolves out of the player's own RA install via the `~*.mix` mounts (`mod.yaml:21-37`) — all 88 music entries bar `journey`, and ~121 of 124 notification sounds (`rules/sound/notifications.yaml` is stock EVA throughout: `baseatk1`, `nofunds1`, `misnwon1`, …). That is at least conditioned on the player owning the game. *(b) Redistributed in-repo:* 270 audio files under `mods/ww3mod/bits/sounds/`, and the directory names give the origin away — `commando/` is Tiberian Dawn's Commando (`ramyell1`, `rrokroll1`, `rtuffguy1`), `glabike/` is Generals' GLA Combat Cycle (`vcyc*`), `v3/` `seal/` `chem/` `terroist/` are Red Alert 2, `robot/` is TS-era (`vsen*`). **RA1 assets can at least gesture at the 2008 freeware release; RA2 and Generals have no such release.** Separately, `bits/sounds/arabs/` (32 files, stock RA lines re-encoded as `.a0X`) is **not mounted in `mod.yaml` and not referenced by any YAML** — verified: no `.a0X` appears in `voices.yaml`, whose variant sets are `.v00-.v03`/`.r00-.r03` (`voices.yaml:3-5, 16-18`). It is unreachable at runtime, so deleting it costs nothing and removes 32 redistributed files.

## 2026-08-11 — a tournament run silently degrades to no-verdict under CPU contention

> **[rejected: operational harness knowledge, not engine/gameplay reference — it belongs in `DOCS/recipes/AUTOTEST.md`, not `DOCS/reference/`. The core finding is real and re-verified (the wall-clock watchdog kills the match and the batch continues, `run-tournament.sh:328-337`; the tally line at `:368`; aggregation runs whenever `OK > 0` at `:373-375`, so a 2-of-10 run produces a full-looking `summary.csv`/`summary.json`). **TWO CLAIMS ARE WRONG, and the second matters:** (a) `--max-wall-secs` is 4×`TimeLimitSeconds` **divided by `SpeedMultiplier`** (`:159-165`), i.e. 4× expected *wall* time, not 4× sim time — self-consistent with the entry's own 150 s observation but not with its sentence; (b) the single-instance lock does **not** cover tournaments — it lives only in `run-test.sh:325-357`, and `run-tournament.sh`/`loop-tournament.sh` have zero references to it, so two concurrent tournaments are unserialized. The entry's “the lock prevents two harness runs from corrupting each other” is true only for `run-test.sh`/`run-batch.sh`.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

**Finding.** `run-tournament.sh` was run on merged main (`63a81fe0`) for 10 seeds of
`tournament-s1-eco-river-zeta` while a worker concurrently ran `dotnet build WW3MOD.sln -c Release`
and `make test` in a separate worktree. Load average reached **16.75**. Matches 1–2 completed
normally (7500 ticks, `time_limit`); matches 3–10 were all killed by the 150 s wall-clock watchdog
with **no verdict file**. Final tally: **2 verdict / 8 no-verdict**.

**Why it matters more than "it was slow".** The failure is not graceful. The wall-clock watchdog
kills the game and the run continues, so the batch still produces a `summary.csv`, a
`summary.json` and a cheerful "Quick view" — containing only the surviving rows. A summary with two
rows in it looks exactly like a summary with ten rows in it unless someone reads the
verdict/no-verdict tally on the line above. **A contaminated benchmark is therefore
indistinguishable from a small one at the point where the numbers get used**, which is precisely how
a bad number enters a decision.

**The watchdog is wall-clock, not work-based.** `--max-wall-secs` defaults to 4x the config's
`TimeLimitSeconds`. At `Test.SpeedMultiplier=8` a 5-minute eco rung should finish in well under a
minute of wall time, so the 4x default looks generous — but it budgets against *elapsed time*, and
elapsed time is a function of how much CPU the rest of the machine is using. The margin evaporates
under a parallel MSBuild (7 nodes observed) plus two `--check-yaml` processes.

**Operational rule this establishes.** Serialising the *harness lock* is not sufficient. The
single-instance lock added on 2026-08-10 prevents two harness runs from corrupting each other, but
it says nothing about builds, test suites or YAML lints running beside a match. Any benchmark or
tournament intended to produce trustworthy numbers must run on a **quiet machine**: no concurrent
build, no `dotnet test`, no `make test`. When a manager owns simulations and workers own builds,
those two must be serialised against each other, not just against themselves.

**Tell.** Read the `Batch complete: N verdict / M no-verdict` line before reading any aggregate. If
M > 0 the run is suspect; if M is most of the batch the aggregate is meaningless regardless of how
plausible the surviving rows look.

## 2026-08-11 — the danger field's absolute magnitude is scenario-dependent, so "17 of 18 thresholds are too low" is not a universal fact

> **[promoted: → influence-stack.md §Stage B — the reference-vs-field distinction and the rule that any “threshold X is too low” claim must name its scenario and match phase. Re-verified: the `[danger] reference` line is unconditional once per world (`DangerFieldLayer.cs:436-446`), while `[danger] dist`/`pct` are gated (`:1103-1106`) — a caveat the entry does not make. **Status of its recommendation banked as OPEN:** percentile instrumentation exists (`LogPercentiles` `:568-583`, nearest-rank `Percentile` `:591-599`), but `GroundDangerMedian` has exactly one caller (`SupplyFollowerBotModule.cs:1373`, via `DropDangerFloorUnits`/`DropDangerMedianPercent`, `ai.yaml:1094-1095`); the other eight gates are still absolute constants spanning 6–100.]** (curation 2026-08-12, verified against main @ 4d3c8f90).

**Source.** Engine `debug.log` from a `tournament-s1-eco-river-zeta` match on merged main
`63a81fe0`. The match itself was killed by the wall-clock watchdog under CPU contention (see the
entry above) — but `[danger]` instrumentation is unconditional, so the diagnostic value survives
the void run.

**The reference reproduces exactly.** `[danger] reference ground=3412 air=3627 ... ground-types=92/424
min=164 max=1271250` — identical in all six published figures to the 2026-08-10 live measurement and
to the offline YAML reproduction in `f2a31035`. The reference is deterministic, ruleset-derived, and
now confirmed from three independent routes. That part of the model is solid.

**The FIELD is not.** Compare the believed-danger distribution measured on the two occasions:

| Source | scenario | USA median | Russia median |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-10 | `test-frontline-reachability` | **818 units** | **2,755 units** |
| 2026-08-11 | `tournament-s1-eco-river-zeta` (n=120→160) | **27–38 units** | **17–99 units** |

That is a **20x–100x** difference in the same quantity on the same map. The thresholds under
discussion span **6–100 danger units**. So on the frontline scenario every threshold sits far below
the median cell — the finding that drove the 08-10 plan — while on this eco rung the same thresholds
**straddle** the median instead.

**Why this matters.** The 08-10 conclusion "17 of the 18 ground thresholds sit 8x–459x below the
median cell they gate" was derived from a single scenario, and it does not generalise. A global
constant cannot be correct for both readings; whatever value makes a gate sensible on a contested
frontline makes it fire on essentially everything during an economic opening, and vice versa. This
is the same argument the inter-player asymmetry already made (USA and Russia medians differing 3.4x
in one match), now repeated along a second axis — **scenario and match phase** — and with a much
larger spread.

**Consequence for the threshold work.** It strengthens the percentile-of-live-field model over any
re-tuned constant, because a percentile is invariant to the absolute scale that is moving here. It
also means any future claim of the form "threshold X is too low" MUST name the scenario and the
match phase it was measured in, or it is not a claim about the threshold at all.

**Caveat, stated plainly.** This is one match, killed early (the highest scan index seen is n=160),
on an economic rung where contact is expected to be sparse. Match phase alone could account for much
of the gap. It is offered as a refutation of universality — one counterexample is sufficient for
that — and NOT as a measurement of what the eco-rung distribution settles at.

## 2026-08-11 — the derrick ferry DOES fire, refuting the cached-null-latch hypothesis
